## 1. Executive opportunity summary

Eight opportunities went into the final gate. Three earned INVEST, two EXPLORE, one WATCH, two REJECT - and the finding that matters most is not the ranking but its shape: none of the three funded items is a new product. OPP-07 The Other Half (rank 1, 68.8) is a women's block-and-proportion input plus two free internal sell-through pulls. OPP-03 Twenty Washes (rank 2, 59.0) is a make standard and a buy discipline on garments already in the line. OPP-02 Found Outdoors (rank 3, 55.5) is a naming, laddering and rack-legibility action on FN2659, a SKU Nike already ships in the doors it needs. All three survive only in DE-SCOPED form; the red team turned each from a franchise into an input. The engine's own conclusion about this category is capture, not invention - the growth it can evidence is in making existing shorts findable, durable, correctly proportioned and correctly sized, not in a new short. That is also the most uncomfortable finding here, because a capture programme produces no image for a line review.

Three structural facts govern everything above. First, the cross-dataset audit found no first-party Nike commercial data anywhere in the base and not one price confirmed against a retrieved page, with three mutually incompatible Nike price ladders coexisting - so every price and every length in all eight briefs is unanchored. Five of eight briefs proposed a new price rung; all have been struck. Second, the systemic failure across all seven specialists, flagged identically by all seven skeptics, was proposing product Nike already ships: the DNA UV Woven (FN2659) alone closed four independently declared white spaces. Third, roughly three quarters of the evidence is US-derived, while the stated SS28 priority space (Worldball, centred on Greater China) rests on evidence sourced almost entirely from outside China.

What needs a human decision: (a) whether to fund a capture portfolio at all when only OPP-07 sits inside a named SS28 space and Uniform of Youth is served by nothing that survived; (b) OPP-06's Doha leg, the only item with an external clock - the FIBA product partnership expires in 2027 with no renewal found, and the LA28 leg is already killed on rights held by Fanatics, Ralph Lauren and FOURTEEN; (c) the EmpCo claims review, applicable 27 September 2026 and now a compliance item regardless of this portfolio; (d) an explicit adjacency plan, because four of eight briefs propose product against the same DNA/Icon rail. The decision gate is open. This document does not close it.

### Market framing

The global basketball shorts market, as evidenced here rather than as assumed: a flat-unit, price-and-mix business meeting a competitive field in retreat, with the shelf already discounting.

Nike's own audited disclosure (A03-S9) shows apparel growing about +2% currency-neutral on units +1%, with ASP growth coming from mix and already eroded by discounts, against roughly USD 1.5B of annualised tariff cost and 120bp of FY26 gross-margin headwind (A04-S8). The channel has inverted: wholesale +4% against ten consecutive quarters of Nike Digital decline (A02-S7, A04-S1, both VERIFIED), while every Western competitor retreats from performance basketball apparel (PAT-10). Greater China is Nike's weakest region in the same filings.

Demand is not uniformly soft. Women's basketball is the one signal the audit made STRONGER: three consecutive record seasons, a ratified CBA, verified Unrivaled event economics including roughly USD 400,000 of merchandise in one Philadelphia night (A05-S7), a retailer CEO's first-party call-out (A04-S5), and registry participation growth in a second country (A02-S9). Heat is the only functional need corroborated across physiology (A06-S2, 0.00-1.33 kg of trapped sweat), documented institutional behaviour change (A06-S5) and a competitor's multi-season commercial platform (A03-S7) - PAT-11.

Against that, the observable shelf refuses price: DNA 8 inch at 50% off, DNA 6 inch realised at USD 37.50, a USD 65 Sabrina clearing at USD 42.97, the Australian UV Woven at AUD 44.99, Kohl's Big and Tall Academy 11 inch at USD 27.75, Decathlon's Tarmak SH500 at GBP 5.99. Critically, no syndicated source isolates basketball shorts as a segment at all (A02-S1 after the audit stripped its CAGR). There is no market size for this category in this base that we would defend.

### The three most consequential opportunities and why each surfaced

#### OPP-07 — The Other Half

**Why it surfaced.** It surfaced by reading the culture domain AGAINST its own conclusion. A05 used 'female jersey outfit' at +494% as proof that consumers want women's basketball SHORTS; the strongest term in the dataset is a TOPS term, and the same Pinterest report shows 'F1 aesthetic outfit' at +483% and 'Brazil jersey outfit women' at +302%, so the wave is pan-sport and the auditor instructed the basketball attribution be dropped. The correct reading only appears when that is placed next to a product-domain finding buried in SKEPTIC counter-evidence - that Sabrina buyers report wearing the short at home more than on court, so the willingness to pay is lifestyle-driven - and next to an event-retail number the culture specialist missed (roughly USD 400,000 of merchandise in one Unrivaled night in Philadelphia). Three files each held a third of it and each drew a performance conclusion. Then the cross-dataset audit did something no specialist could: it replaced the 2024 WNBA press release that three domains were double-counting with 2026 evidence, which converted the case from 'explosive spike on a soft base, with live labour risk' into three consecutive seasons of growth under a ratified CBA, achieved with the concentration athlete sidelined. That is the only signal in the entire pipeline the audit made STRONGER.

**Domains that converged.** Culture (A05-S7 verified Unrivaled event economics, A05-S4 platform search behaviour, A05-S1 supply-chain read), commercial (A04-S5, a retailer CEO's first-party call-out on his own earnings call), marketplace (A02-S9, registry participation in a second country with no connection to any US league, and A02-S7's verified wholesale swing), consumer (A01-S1, a large teen panel showing Nike's female mindshare falling), and product (A03-S6, the actual reported use occasion of an existing women's SKU) - five domains, four instruments sharing no source, pointing one direction on demand and the opposite direction on the product conclusion drawn from it.

**What makes it consequential.** It is the only item on the board where the demand half is settled rather than argued and Nike's position is exclusive rather than merely strong - Nike designs the WNBA on-court uniform, holds Sabrina and A'ja Wilson, adds Caitlin Clark from 1 October 2026, and is the only party controlling trim, placket, colour standard and drop calendar on BOTH halves of the outfit. An individual PLM would have seen 'women's basketball is hot' and briefed a women's shorts programme - three specialists did exactly that and all three were rejected for claiming an empty category. What no individual would have seen is the two-sided correction: that the fixture is already built and already stocked with three Nike shorts at USD 49.99-85 (so the opportunity is not a franchise), AND that none of them is built on a high-rise, jersey-tucking women's block (so there is still a real proposition). The consequence is a cheap, precise ask in the one named SS28 priority space, gated on two pulls Nike already owns - and a live unresolved fork about whether the block is women's-graded or unisex that the pipeline was honest enough not to close.

#### OPP-03 — Twenty Washes

**Why it surfaced.** It surfaced because four functions that never meet each held one quarter of it and each quarter looked like noise alone: review sentiment sits with consumer experience, markdown depth with sales, fabric GSM history with materials, and the composition of ASP growth with finance. The failure mode was also actively mis-diagnosed inside the base - the consumer domain built a pocket-engineering recommendation on one unverified snippet while the same review corpus reproducibly complained about SEAMS and SHRINKAGE - and the single usable quality datapoint in 58 signals (Dick's Icon+ 6 inch at 3.9 stars, 67% recommending across 64 reviews) was found by a SKEPTIC, not a specialist. Then the red team tried to kill it as a review-venue artifact and instead reproduced the same defect language on a DIFFERENT SKU (Icon 11 inch) at a THIRD retailer, which made it the only reproducible consumer finding in the entire base and one of only two kill attempts in the whole pipeline that failed outright. Separately, nobody had costed the liner, and nobody had noticed that the physiological argument (densest wet mass in a garment trapping up to 1.33 kg of sweat), the competitive-rules argument (compression under the short is legal at any length) and the P&L argument all point at deleting the same component from three unconnected files.

**Domains that converged.** Consumer (A01-S3 the Walmart review corpus, A04-S6 the Dick's corpus found by the skeptic), commercial (A03-S9, audited disclosure that apparel growth is price-and-mix with units +1%; A04-S8 the tariff and margin headwind; A02-S7 the verified channel swing), athlete (A06-S3 and A06-S6 primary FIBA and NFHS rule text on compression legality; A06-S2 peer-reviewed trapped-sweat measurement), and marketplace (A02-S4 the markdown structure). Five domains, and the liner-deletion mechanism only exists at their intersection - it is simultaneously a physiology finding, a rules finding and a funding mechanism.

**What makes it consequential.** It carries the highest confidence on the board, it creates margin without creating inventory, and every decisive test uses data Nike already owns with an explicit stop-gate - the best risk-adjusted dollar in the portfolio. An individual PLM would never brief this: it changes no silhouette, adds no length, adds no SKU, opens no market, sits outside all three SS28 priority spaces, produces no image for a line review, and would be executed by Materials, Sourcing and Quality rather than by PLM. The design director ranked it fifth for precisely those reasons and he is right that it is table stakes rather than a bet. It is consequential anyway, for two reasons that only appear at portfolio level: no premium tier survives on a core that fails after one wash, so it is the precondition for the rest of the ladder; and the red team's sharpest correction on it - that the USD 19 'whole business case' is a RETAIL markdown booked into a 70/30 WHOLESALE-weighted programme, so part of it is a gift to Foot Locker - is a P&L-level error that would have shipped unchallenged in any single-owner brief.

#### OPP-02 — Found Outdoors

**Why it surfaced.** It surfaced as a measurement of the pipeline itself. Three independent domains each concluded that outdoor function, secure storage and UPF were unowned white space - and one live inline SKU, the Nike DNA Dri-FIT 6 inch UV Woven (FN2659), closes all three at once with UVA/UVB protection, side pockets, a phone-secure zippered pocket and a rebound-durability claim. That is one un-run catalogue query counted three times, not three findings, and no researcher can observe their own blind spot: the FAILURE of seven researchers to find a product they had no trouble finding at Li-Ning is itself the data. The genuinely open technical question then sits between two literatures that never cite each other - a physiology paper measuring 0.00-1.33 kg of sweat trapped in a basketball uniform, and a textile paper showing 100% polyester already rates UPF 40-50 DRY with moisture as the untested variable. Read separately they are two reasons NOT to build anything; only together do they say the category's sun claim is measured in a state the player is never in. The red team then closed even that door by retrieving AATCC 183 and ASTM D6603, which already provide the wet and stretched protocols - turning the moat into a purchasable test election.

**Domains that converged.** Product (A03-S7 Li-Ning's multi-season Wade UPF 50+ commercial platform; A03-S4 Nike's declared cooling vector), athlete (A06-S2 peer-reviewed trapped-sweat physiology; A06-S5 documented institutional behaviour change in the Philippines, where meets moved off the 9am-3pm window from 2024; A06-S7 textile UV chemistry; A06-S4 storage), design (A07-S8 the composed outdoor system; A07-S9 competitors printing function on the outside of the garment), marketplace and commercial (A02-S7 and A04-S1, the verified wholesale swing against ten consecutive quarters of Nike Digital decline), and consumer (A01-S7, the S.T. Flare precedent - Nike has already made this consumer argument one category over). Six domains, three of which independently produced the same false white space.

**What makes it consequential.** It is the only candidate that is genuinely multi-region and multi-season on day one, on a garment that already exists in the doors it needs - so it is the highest-productivity move available to a line planner and it needs no research gate. But its real consequence is the lesson it forces on the whole organisation: the binding constraint in this category is legibility and distribution, not capability. An individual PLM sitting in one geography would have briefed an outdoor innovation programme - three specialists did - and would not have seen that Nike already ships the product, that the differentiator is a test election any competitor buys in one cycle, that per-colourway UPF certification is economically incompatible with the seasonal graphic strategy in the same brief, that a private label already sells the exact feature stack at 5/7/9 inseams on Amazon, or that Nike's own claims policy declines to print a UPF number even in Australia. What survives is smaller and cheaper than the brief and more valuable than the invention it replaced - which is the shape of almost everything that survived this pipeline.

### How to read confidence

Three different confidence numbers appear in this pipeline and they are not interchangeable. Read them in this order.

1. DEVELOPMENT confidence (0-100), set by the agent that wrote the brief, before challenge. Range here: 34 (OPP-05) to 62 (OPP-02). Treat as an author's self-assessment.

2. ADJUSTED confidence, set by the red-team challenger after attacking the brief. Every single one fell: OPP-01 52 to 26, OPP-02 62 to 40, OPP-03 60 to 48, OPP-04 61 to 38, OPP-05 34 to 24, OPP-06 57 to 39, OPP-07 61 to 41, OPP-08 58 to 44. Only OPP-01 was declared dead (survives=false). The uniform decline is the most honest number in the file: no brief got stronger under attack, and the average drop is roughly 17 points.

3. PORTFOLIO confidence, set by the ranking chair on the de-scoped version of each brief, which is why it can sit above the adjusted score (OPP-03 at 62 versus an adjusted 48). It answers 'how sure am I of the thing I am actually funding', not 'how sure am I of the brief as written'.

Four cautions. First, CONFIDENCE AND RANK MEASURE DIFFERENT THINGS and are deliberately allowed to disagree: OPP-03 carries the portfolio's highest confidence (62) and ranks second, while OPP-07 ranks first at 58. Anyone re-weighting toward certainty and away from newness should reverse the top two, and the portfolio says so (D-07). Second, THERE IS A CEILING: nothing exceeds 62, and no opportunity scores above 3 on risk. That is a portfolio-wide floor reflecting the unanchored evidence base, not a per-brief penalty. Third, CONFIDENCE IS NOT INDEPENDENT ACROSS ITEMS: most of these scores would move together on the same three or four internal data pulls, so they are correlated, not eight separate bets. Fourth, HIGH CONFIDENCE IS NOT A DECISION - OPP-08 carries confidence 50 and remains EXPLORE because the cheap kill test has not been run.

Finally: every claim in this portfolio is labelled either as a FINDING (evidenced, cited by signal id) or a HYPOTHESIS (inferred, uncorroborated). Where a brief's central premise is a hypothesis, it is said so explicitly - that outdoor findability rather than function is the binding constraint (OPP-02), that jersey-adjacency drives a bottoms purchase (OPP-07), that fabric GSM ever changed (OPP-03). Do not read those as facts because they sit inside a funded item.

## 2. Ranked product opportunities (INVEST / EXPLORE / WATCH / REJECT)

Three rankers scored eight opportunities and returned three different top-threes. That is the useful part. The PLM director led with OPP-07, the commercial planner with OPP-03, the design director with OPP-07 but with OPP-06 second and OPP-03 fifth. Where they agree, the finding is robust. Where they split, I have decided rather than averaged, and the splits are recorded below.

My own weights sit between theirs and I state them so the arithmetic is auditable: commercial potential 15, consumer need 13, evidence strength 13, product differentiation 11, Nike right to win 10, scalability 10, market whitespace 7, cultural relevance 7, basketball authenticity 7, risk 7 (5 = low risk). Overall = sum of weight x (score-1)/4, so a straight 3 across the board scores 50, not 60. I adopted the design director's calibration deliberately: this evidence base does not deserve a scale on which mediocrity averages into a pass.

Four things govern every category call. First, the cross-dataset audit is blunt that there is no first-party Nike commercial data anywhere in the base, that not one price was confirmed against a retrieved page, and that three mutually incompatible Nike price ladders coexist. Every price and every length in all eight briefs is therefore unanchored. Second, the systemic failure across seven specialists - flagged identically by all seven skeptics - was proposing product Nike already ships; the DNA UV Woven (FN2659) alone closed four independently declared white spaces. Differentiation here means newness against Nike's own live line, and it scores low across the board for good reason. Third, category answers 'what does the next dollar buy', not 'what is the composite'. Fourth, and most consequential: every one of my three INVESTs survives only in DE-SCOPED form. The red team turned each of them from a franchise into an input. That is the engine working, and it means the SS28 ask is far smaller and far cheaper than the briefs propose.

OPP-07 The Other Half ranks first at 68.8 because it is the only place where the demand half is settled rather than argued and where Nike's position is exclusive rather than merely strong. Women's basketball is the one signal the audit made STRONGER - three consecutive record seasons, an All-Star crowd of 19,783 outdrawing the NBA's, a ratified CBA with the team cap up roughly fivefold, and growth achieved with Caitlin Clark sidelined - and only Nike controls the trim, colour standard and drop calendar on both halves of the outfit. The challenger took 20 points off and never touched the demand. What he did destroy is the fixture premise: the Ladies WNBA bottoms fixture is already built and already stocked with three Nike shorts. So I fund the block-and-proportion work and two free first-party pulls. I do not fund the franchise, the USD 65-75 rung argued off a wall discounting 25-45%, or an unbuyable six-dimensional SKU matrix. The commercial planner voted EXPLORE on exactly those grounds and I have adopted his de-scope inside an INVEST.

OPP-03 Twenty Washes ranks second at 59.0 with the portfolio's highest confidence, 62. It is the only reproducible consumer finding in 58 signals, it got stronger under attack, it creates margin without creating inventory, and every decisive test uses data Nike already owns. The design director ranked it fifth and he is right about why: it builds no identity and sits outside all three SS28 spaces. I am funding it anyway, because it consumes no line slot and line-plan productivity precedes newness. But the badge does not ship, the guarantee does not ship, and the USD 19 case is re-modelled at Nike realised wholesale revenue before anything else happens.

OPP-02 Found Outdoors ranks third at 55.5 on scalability - the only genuinely multi-region, multi-season candidate on day one, on a garment already in the doors it needs. I buy the naming, laddering and rack-legibility programme. I refuse the wet-and-stretched UPF certification, which AATCC 183 and ASTM D6603 already cover and any competitor can elect in one cycle.

Below the line: OPP-08 EXPLORE on a near-free test; OPP-06 EXPLORE on the Doha leg only, and it is the single item on this board with an external clock; OPP-04 WATCH, its proving-ground mechanism arithmetically void; OPP-01 and OPP-05 REJECT, one already on the order form it proposes to build, the other differentiating on a regulation everyone clears by staying silent.

### Where the rankers disagreed (preserved, not averaged)

- **D-01.** OPP-07 category. The PLM director and the design director both ranked it FIRST and voted INVEST; the commercial planner scored it second-highest of anything on his board (67.0) and still voted EXPLORE. His objection is specific and correct: the Ladies WNBA bottoms fixture is already built and already stocked with three Nike shorts at USD 49.99-85, the USD 65-75 rung rests on a wall discounting 25-45% against a Sabrina realising USD 42.97, and the specced matrix - two fabrics x two inseams x XS-3X-plus-tall x four core colours x three drop windows x per-tour-stop exclusives - is an unbuyable size curve. The PLM and design cases rest on something the challenger never attacked: none of the three incumbent Nike shorts is built on a high-rise, jersey-tucking women's block, and rise and leg-line are a design proposition rather than a fourth SKU. _Resolution:_ INVEST, scoped to the intersection of all three positions rather than to any one of them. I fund the block-and-proportion input and the two free first-party pulls (Rebel Fanwear and Caitlin Clark sell-through; bottoms share of women's fan units). I do not fund the franchise, the fixture ask, the USD 65-75 rung or the SKU matrix. The commercial planner's de-scope is adopted in full INSIDE an INVEST, because the demand pool is the only settled one on the board and the scoped ask is nearly free. If the pulls show fan bottoms are a small, discounting share of that wall, this drops to a proportion revision inside programmes already funded, and I have said so in the key dependency rather than burying it.

- **D-02.** OPP-03 rank. It carries the highest adjusted confidence in the portfolio (48) and the commercial planner ranked it first (71.4) and the PLM director second (67.6). The design director ranked it FIFTH (48.8) and explicitly flagged the departure: the brief keeps silhouettes deliberately unchanged so the only variable in market is the make, so it builds no visual identity, recruits no athlete, tells no story a consumer repeats, and sits outside all three SS28 priority spaces by its own admission. On his board it scores 1 on cultural relevance and 2 on differentiation, and those carry 30 of his 100 points. _Resolution:_ Rank 2, INVEST, with the highest confidence score on the board (62) - and I am deliberately letting rank and confidence disagree, because they measure different things. The design director is right that this is table stakes executed well, not a bet, and my weights (18 combined on differentiation and cultural relevance) are what pull it below OPP-07. But it consumes no line slot, so it does not compete with OPP-07 or OPP-02 for a place in the line, and no premium tier survives on a core that fails after one wash. It is funded, and the badge and the guarantee are both killed. Not averaged: the disagreement is a weighting difference between chairs, not a factual one, and it is preserved as such.

- **D-03.** OPP-05 category. The commercial planner and the design director both voted REJECT (39.6 and 25.8, the latter the lowest score any ranker gave anything). The PLM director voted EXPLORE at 45.8, explicitly not on the composite but on the grounds that 'category answers what the next dollar buys' and what this brief actually asks for is a minimum viable European read - the same read the cross-dataset audit independently instructed before ranking. All three agree the garment is duplicative and the moat inverts; they disagree only on whether the research gate needs an opportunity wrapped around it. _Resolution:_ REJECT the opportunity; ELEVATE the research gate to a portfolio-level mandated action independent of any brief. The PLM's substantive point is upheld and the vehicle is rejected. Two actions are carried forward regardless: the EmpCo legal review (time-critical at roughly three weeks out, required for OPP-02 and OPP-03 anyway), and a minimum viable European read whose first and cheapest query is Nike's own live EMEA basketball assortment, SKU count, inseam mix and price ladder. I chose rejection over EXPLORE because an EXPLORE label on a franchise brief is how a EUR 45 rung, a 27-jurisdiction claims architecture and a governed markdown floor get funded in the one region where Nike's results show it cannot hold price.

- **D-04.** OPP-06 rank and category - the widest split in the exercise. The design director ranked it SECOND at 68.8 (EXPLORE, time-critical), citing the confirmed FIBA product partnership, the TRANSIT numbered-drop chassis as genuine brand architecture, and dated moments as the only proven full-price mechanism in a flat-unit business. The commercial planner ranked it SIXTH at 45.6 and voted WATCH, calling a dated, non-replenishable capsule at USD 55-85 with no reorder path 'the worst inventory shape in the file' (scalability 1, risk 1). The PLM director sat between them at 50.0 EXPLORE and split the programme in two: Doha is inside confirmed rights, LA28 belongs to Fanatics, Ralph Lauren and FOURTEEN. _Resolution:_ EXPLORE, scoped to the Doha leg alone, gated on two zero-cost internal reads, and flagged TIME-CRITICAL. The LA28 / VALLEY leg is killed today on rights, not on evidence. Rank 5 at 44.3 - I have kept the commercial planner's scalability 2 and risk 2 rather than the design director's 3 and 2, because a non-replenishable capsule genuinely is the structural opposite of franchise potential; but I have kept differentiation at 3 rather than 2 because the numbered-drop chassis is a real construct and not feature stacking. The decisive fact neither the composite nor the confidence score captures is that this is the only item on the board with an external clock: the FIBA agreement expires in 2027 with no renewal found, so the leg with rights is closing while nobody decides. That is why it sits at EXPLORE and not WATCH despite the inventory shape.

- **D-05.** OPP-02 category. The PLM director (66.4) and commercial planner (63.8) both voted INVEST; the design director voted EXPLORE at 57.0, on the grounds that the challenger removed the only thing that made it a franchise rather than a fix - the wet-and-stretched UPF certification is a purchasable test election, not a first, and the feature composition already ships at private-label price with 'basketball' in the title. _Resolution:_ INVEST at the de-scoped version only. All three rankers described the SAME de-scoped programme - name and ladder FN2659, add a knee-clearing 9 inch and a boys' 5 inch, extend the women's block, build the legibility system, hold price - and disagreed only on whether that earns an INVEST label. I have given it one because it needs no research gate and carries essentially zero incremental inventory liability: the garment exists and is already stocked in the doors it needs. The certification programme and the price-up are explicitly not funded, which is the design director's objection honoured in the scope rather than in the label. Separately noted and not resolved: the design director found that the proposed heritage naming route names a Reebok trademark, so the franchise cannot be called what the brief wants to call it.

- **D-06.** OPP-04 category. The commercial planner voted EXPLORE at 54.0 (his highest score for anything below the top three, driven by evidence strength 4); the PLM director and design director both voted WATCH at 46.8 and 44.8. All three agree the proving-ground mechanism is arithmetically void - the SS28 buy closes around the month the Australian range would land - and all three agree the right action is to pull eight quarters of existing Nike AU sell-through from Rebel, JD and Foot Locker AU. _Resolution:_ WATCH. The disagreement reduces to whether that pull is a programme or a phone call, and it is a phone call. There is no dollar to spend here: the pull belongs to OPP-02's owner and Australia is instrumented as a lead door inside the global franchise rather than as a separate slot. I also overrode all three rankers downward on one criterion - nike_right_to_win scored 2, following the PLM's finding that Nike holds no Australian basketball rights at all (iAthletic for the Boomers and Opals, Champion for the NBL, Foot Locker sponsoring the Boomers), which removes the women's-colourway platform and the on-court surround the brief leans on. That is what separates it from OPP-06 at the same raw composite.

- **D-07.** Structural weighting disagreement between the three chairs, which is not an error and should not be reconciled. The commercial planner put 7 of 100 points on basketball authenticity and cultural relevance combined and said so on the record as a deliberate disagreement with the brand lens; the design director put 27 on the same two, plus 16 on differentiation, and said averaging his board with the others would erase the signal he was spawned to produce. The PLM director sat between, weighting scalability hardest and down-weighting market whitespace on the grounds that whitespace claims in this base are mostly search artifacts. _Resolution:_ Not resolvable, and deliberately preserved. My chair weights (commercial potential 15, consumer need 13, evidence strength 13, differentiation 11, right to win 10, scalability 10, whitespace 7, cultural relevance 7, authenticity 7, risk 7) sit between theirs and are stated so the arithmetic is auditable. The visible consequence is the OPP-07 / OPP-03 ordering: on the commercial planner's weights OPP-03 wins, on the design director's OPP-07 wins by 25 points, and on mine OPP-07 wins by 9.8 with OPP-03 carrying the higher confidence. Anyone re-weighting toward certainty and away from newness should reverse the top two, and that is a legitimate reading rather than a mistake.

- **D-08.** Inseam direction, unresolved across the entire pipeline and load-bearing under OPP-08, OPP-02 and OPP-07. A07-S4 argues design at the poles (a short-inseam performance wave among named NBA players); A02-S5's own cited source says modern performance shorts run 7-9 inches, contradicting its own headline; the auditor rated both the short-inseam wave and the retro/long swingman trend UNCLEAR and struck the entire Accio-generated quantitative spine of the latter; and Nike's live ladder runs 6-11 inches continuously with the longest length at the lowest price. _Resolution:_ Carried forward unresolved and explicitly NOT averaged into a length recommendation. Unit share by inseam appears nowhere in seven specialist files, three skeptic rounds or the cross-dataset audit, in any market. No opportunity in this portfolio may be built on a length assumption until that pull exists; it is the first line of the portfolio-level data request and it is the number OPP-08 turns on.

- **D-09.** OPP-07 block definition: women's-graded or unisex. The PLM director surfaced a fork nobody resolved - Ed Stack described 'boys and girls, young men and women' buying this product on his own earnings call (A04-S5), which argues a unisex fan block offered in a women's size run rather than a women's-graded block. The brief, the challenge and the other two rankers all assume a women's-graded block. _Resolution:_ Unresolved and preserved as an open fork inside a funded item, not decided by the chair. It is answerable from the same two free pulls that gate the whole opportunity - if the Rebel Fanwear and Clark short sell-through skews cross-gender, the block is unisex in a women's size run. Deciding it in this document on no evidence would be exactly the kind of silent averaging this pipeline exists to prevent.

- **D-10.** OPP-08 scalability. The PLM director scored it 2 - the score that kept it out of his top three - because the Nike UK ladder does not reproduce the US shape, so the inversion may be a US price-file artifact rather than a global architecture problem. The commercial planner scored it 4, because the action rides an existing block, carries over and reorders, which is precisely the shape he rewards. The design director scored 3. _Resolution:_ Final score 3, which is not a split-the-difference but a statement that both are true of different halves of the brief: the ARCHITECTURE claim does not scale on one market's price file (PLM correct), while the ACTION - listing an 11 inch inside the premium DNA franchise in existing fabric - rides an existing global block and reorders (commercial planner correct). The EXPLORE scope funds the second and not the first, which is why the score sits in the middle rather than at either pole.

### Portfolio observations

- OVER-INVESTMENT IN ASP. Five of eight briefs proposed a new price rung and not one anchored it to a retrieved Nike price file - the audit found three mutually incompatible Nike price ladders coexisting in the base and not one price confirmed against a page. Meanwhile every observable shelf is discounting: DNA 8 inch at 50% off, DNA 6 inch realised at USD 37.50, Sabrina's USD 65 clearing at USD 42.97, the Australian UV Woven at AUD 44.99 against an AUD 75-80 ask, Kohl's Big and Tall Academy 11 inch at USD 27.75. In a business growing +2% currency-neutral on units +1%, an unanchored price-up is not upside, it is an unbooked markdown. Every price in all three surviving INVESTs has therefore been struck, and each is funded on a mechanism that does not require the consumer to pay more.
- THE PORTFOLIO'S OWN CONCLUSION IS CAPTURE, NOT INVENTION. Nothing that survived is a new thing. OPP-02 is a naming, laddering and legibility action on a SKU Nike already ships in the doors it needs; OPP-03 is a make standard on garments already in the line; OPP-07 is a block-and-proportion input into programmes already funded; OPP-08 is a listing decision inside an existing franchise. All three INVESTs survive only in DE-SCOPED form - the red team turned each from a franchise into an input. That is the single most important thing this exercise found about the category: the growth is not in a new short, it is in making the existing ones findable, durable, correctly proportioned and correctly sized. It is also the pipeline's most uncomfortable finding, because a capture programme produces no image for a line review.
- ONE DATA REQUEST UNBLOCKS HALF THE BOARD. OPP-02, OPP-03, OPP-04 and OPP-08 all resolve on the same three internal pulls: unit share by inseam (by gender, by market), realised ASP and markdown rate by door, and returns/warranty by defect code. Add a fourth for OPP-07 - Rebel Fanwear and Caitlin Clark shorts sell-through and the bottoms share of women's fan units - and a fifth for OPP-06 - whether the Paris 2024 and 2023 World Cup basketball BOTTOMS cleared at markdown. All five are data Nike already owns, obtainable in weeks at essentially zero external cost. The audit's blunt finding is that there is no first-party Nike commercial data anywhere in this base; five of eight briefs were talked down by the red team for reasons these pulls would settle in either direction. This is the highest-leverage action on the board and it costs time, not money.
- SEQUENCING: EXACTLY ONE ITEM HAS AN EXTERNAL CLOCK. Everything on this board can wait a quarter for data except OPP-06's Doha leg, which sits inside a FIBA product partnership that expires in 2027 with no renewal found - the leg Nike owns is closing while the leg being sold as the destination (LA28) belongs to Fanatics, Ralph Lauren and FOURTEEN. Kill LA28 today and decide Doha this quarter, or it decides itself. Second clock, smaller but real: the EU EmpCo directive applies 27 September 2026, roughly three weeks out, which makes the claims review a prerequisite for OPP-02 and OPP-03 rather than a Continental-specific task. Correct order of operations: internal pulls now (weeks), EmpCo review now (weeks), OPP-02 ladder and legibility into the SS28 assortment (no gate), OPP-03 re-model and audit (gate), OPP-07 block work after the sell-through pulls, OPP-08 one-season 11 inch listing, Doha decision this quarter.
- GEOGRAPHIC INVERSION, UNCORRECTED. Roughly three quarters of the evidence base is US-derived. Europe - Nike's second geography, with EuroLeague at a fourth consecutive attendance record of 3,251,706 (+8%) and TV viewership up 82% to 122.8M - is the primary market of under 2% of signals and enters only as a compliance deadline, a markdown line and a set of doors; its only brief was rejected here. Latin America is absent entirely. The Gulf appears once, as a property blog, while the SS28 window's largest owned basketball moment lands in Doha. Greater China carries the stated priority space on evidence sourced almost entirely from OUTSIDE China - European and US resellers, a JD aggregator, 2023 state media about one village, a 2019 NBA PR estimate - with no Tmall, JD, Douyin or Xiaohongshu datapoint and not one retrieved Chinese price anywhere. Australia, the best-verified non-US market in the base, supports one opportunity and it is a WATCH. The portfolio is weighted inversely to the quality of its own evidence, and this ranking does not fully correct that; it names it.
- THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE LAYER CARRIES THE WEAKEST OPPORTUNITIES. The audit identifies the peer-reviewed physiology, biomechanics and primary rule text in A06-S1, A06-S2 and A06-S3 as the only named-sample, dated, peer-reviewed material in 58 signals, surviving attack essentially intact - and as the layer with the fewest opportunities built on it. The two items built most directly on it, OPP-01 and OPP-06, rank 7th and 5th. Conversely the one signal the audit made STRONGER rather than weaker (women's basketball, reclassified as sustained across three seasons with the CBA risk now settled) carries the number-one item. Both facts should be read as instructions for the next cycle: the rules-and-physiology layer deserves a brief written by someone who was not trying to justify a garment, and the women's demand pool deserves the product work that this pipeline could only scope.
- PRIORITY-SPACE MISALIGNMENT IS INFORMATION, NOT AN ERROR. Only OPP-07 sits squarely inside a named SS28 space (Women's Revolution). Worldball Innovation is served by OPP-02, but as capture rather than innovation - and its centre of gravity is Greater China, where this base holds no price and no sell-through. Uniform of Youth is served by nothing that survived. The two items with the highest confidence scores (OPP-03 at 62 and OPP-08 at 50) sit outside all three spaces by their own admission. Read as a finding rather than a failure: the priority spaces describe where Nike wants to create, and the evidence describes where Nike is currently losing full-price productivity on what it already makes. Those are different lists this season, and pretending otherwise would mean funding the weaker briefs.
- CANNIBALISATION AND DOUBLE-BUYING ARE THE PORTFOLIO'S QUIET RISK. Four of eight briefs propose product against the same DNA/Icon rail. OPP-05 duplicated OPP-03's wash standard and OPP-02's UV claim outright at lower confidence, which is why it was rejected rather than parked. OPP-06 stripped of its date is OPP-01 plus OPP-02 plus OPP-07/08 competing for one buy. OPP-08's 11 inch would hang beside a USD 27.75 Academy 11 inch in the same door, same silhouette, same palette. OPP-07's block risks splitting demand three ways against Clark, Sabrina and Rebel Edition programmes already funded, in a +1% unit environment. Any two of these funded without an explicit adjacency plan buy the same demand twice - which is precisely how a line loses productivity while adding SKUs.
- RISK IS SYSTEMIC HERE, NOT OPPORTUNITY-SPECIFIC. No opportunity on this board scores above 3 on risk, and that is deliberate. The audit established that no product-level evidence exists anywhere in this base in any geography - no shorts unit share by inseam, no price ladder in China, no European consumer read, no realised ASP - so every price position and every length recommendation in all eight briefs shares one unanchored foundation. Layered on top: roughly USD 1.5B of annualised tariff cost and 120bp of FY26 gross-margin headwind, a Piper Sandler reading of Nike teen APPAREL mindshare at 26% with female share below 40% for the first time since 2020, and EmpCo turning durability claims from puffery into sanctionable statements. The honest way to price that is a portfolio-wide risk floor rather than a penalty on individual briefs - and it is why the three INVESTs are all funded on internal data and existing garments rather than on new commitments.

## 3. Human decisions required

The engine stops here. For each opportunity: what the machine knows (evidence-supported), what it believes (interpretation), and what only a human can decide.

### OPP-07 — The Other Half (INVEST)

**What the machine knows**
- [FACT] Women's basketball demand is durable rather than spiky: 2026 was a third consecutive record WNBA season on a per-game basis (approx. 11,381 average across 59 games, vs 10,986 in 2025 and 9,807 in 2024), the All-Star Game drew 19,783 at the United Center and outdrew the NBA's for the first time, and the league reported 73 million unique viewers at the halfway point - achieved with Caitlin Clark sidelined for much of the season, which stress-tests the single-athlete concentration risk in the field. _(A05-S1, A05-S7, A04-S5, A01-S1)_
- [FACT] Live women's basketball event retail converts at the till at a measurable scale: Unrivaled's Philadelphia stop on 30 January 2026 drew 21,490 (a professional women's regular-season record) and generated roughly USD 1M in tickets plus USD 400,000 in merchandise in one night, with season ticket revenue +204% and tickets sold +249%. A05-S7 is VERIFIED. _(A05-S7)_
- [FACT] The labour risk that was live when the source files were written has cleared: a seven-year WNBA CBA covering 2026-2032 has been ratified with the 2026 team salary cap at approximately USD 7.0M, up roughly fivefold and adjusting annually with revenue. A line planned to a women's basketball calendar now has a seven-year calendar. _(A04-S5, A05-S7)_
- [FACT] The opportunity's own stated kill condition is already met, in the wrong direction. The brief says 'if the fixture change cannot be secured, the product should not be made, because the fixture IS the opportunity' - but a dedicated Ladies WNBA Shorts fixture already exists at the largest fan retailer, inside the same storefront as the jerseys, and is stocked substantially with Nike product: Legends Flow Mesh USD 74.99, Legends Relaxed Fit Fleece USD 74.99, 2026 On-Court Dri-FIT Victory USD 84.99, Logowoman Team 13 Crossover USD 49.99, Team 13 Tri-Blend 8in biker USD 79.99; Nike's own WNBA pages carry Victory knee-length USD 85, Basketball Fleece USD 75, Crossover WNBA USD 60; and Rebel Fanwear shorts have been in fan doors since 8 May 2026. CAVEAT ON EVIDENCE GRADE: every retail domain was egress-blocked in the challenge session, so all of these are search-result summaries, not retrieved product pages - confirmable by one buyer walking one Dick's fan wall in an afternoon. _(A03-S6, A03-S4, A02-S7)_
- [FACT] Nike is not entering an empty category. Nike already ships ISoFly, Crossover, Fly Crossover, Sabrina, Sabrina 4 Aero-FIT, WNBA Victory and WNBA Rebel Fanwear women's shorts, plus a plus-size Sabrina SKU (FB8427), and the Caitlin Clark apparel collection already pairs a logo tee with a logo short. Three specialist opportunities in this pipeline claimed the women's category was empty and all three were rejected on audit for exactly this reason. _(A03-S6, A03-S4, A07-S6)_
- [FACT] The proposed USD 65-75 rung is contradicted on BOTH walls. Nike's own Sabrina Dri-FIT Reversible at a USD 65 list was observed clearing at USD 42.97; the fan wall the brief uses as its higher anchor is itself discounting 25-45% with codes (Logowoman Crossover USD 34.97 from USD 49.99; Tri-Blend biker USD 55.99 from USD 79.99; On-Court Victory USD 45.49-64.99 from USD 84.99). The fan fixture raises the LIST ticket, not the realised take. _(A03-S6, A04-S4, A03-S9)_
- [FACT] There is no rising tide to price into: Nike FY2026 apparel was USD 13.4B, +2% currency-neutral on units +1%, with ASP contributing about 1 point sourced from product mix and already partially offset by higher discounts and channel mix - against roughly USD 1.5B of annualised tariff cost and 120bp of FY26 gross-margin headwind. In a +1% unit environment a fourth women's fan short is substitutional unless it demonstrably adds a buyer. _(A03-S9, A04-S8, A04-S4)_
- [FACT] The channel is moving toward the doors this product needs: Nike wholesale grew 4% in Q4 and full-year FY26 while Nike Digital declined for a tenth consecutive quarter, and the retailer that now owns both Dick's and Foot Locker publicly attributed a basketball recovery to women's basketball across both banners on his own earnings call, describing the buyer as 'boys and girls, young men and women'. A02-S7 is VERIFIED; A04-S5's surviving content is the dated first-party quote, not its numbers. _(A02-S7, A04-S5, A04-S1)_
- [FACT] Nike's licence position on both halves of the outfit is exclusive: it designs and supplies the WNBA on-court uniform including the 2026 Rebel Edition programme, holds Sabrina and A'ja Wilson signature lines, adds Caitlin Clark, and put Aero-FIT on a women's-athlete-led signature short and jersey first (17 July 2026). Mitchell & Ness holds a retro fan bottom at USD 80 with no current on-court top; Fanatics distributes at scale but does not design the block; adidas and Puma hold no WNBA on-court licence. _(A03-S4, A03-S6, A07-S6, A05-S1)_
- [FACT] Nike's standing with this exact consumer is falling, not rising. Piper Sandler spring 2025 (n=6,455 teens) showed a 13-point drop in female mindshare with female share under 40% for the first time since 2020; the widely-quoted 49% is FOOTWEAR mindshare while teen APPAREL mindshare is 26%; fall-2025 coverage attributed the subsequent stabilisation to the MALE upper-income bracket while stating share among girls was still declining. The spring 2026 wave exists and was never consulted. _(A01-S1)_
- [PATTERN] PATTERN across five domains that share no source: culture (A05-S7 verified event economics, A05-S4 platform search behaviour, A05-S1 supply-chain read), commercial (A04-S5 a retailer chairman's first-party call-out), marketplace (A02-S9 registry participation in a second country with no connection to any US league; A02-S7 verified wholesale swing), consumer (A01-S1 a large teen panel) and product (A03-S6 the actual reported use occasion of an existing SKU) all point the same direction on DEMAND and the opposite direction on the PRODUCT conclusion three specialists drew from it. This is the only signal in the whole pipeline the cross-dataset audit made STRONGER rather than weaker. _(A05-S7, A05-S4, A05-S1, A04-S5, A02-S9, A02-S7, A01-S1, A03-S6)_
- [PATTERN] PATTERN: the evidence base cannot answer the question this opportunity turns on. There is no first-party Nike commercial data anywhere in the base - no shorts unit share by inseam, no realised ASP, no markdown rate by door, no size-curve fill, no return reasons, in any geography, for either gender - and no measurement anywhere of bottoms as a share of women's basketball fan merchandise. Public-web queries on the question surface Accio (an Alibaba AI B2B sourcing engine) SEO pages, the same laundering path the audit identified behind A04-S5's struck numbers. _(A04-S8, A02-S7, A04-S5, A05-S1)_
- [PATTERN] PATTERN: the cultural attribution is pan-sport, not basketball. The strongest term in the base is 'female jersey outfit' at +494% - a TOPS term - and the same Pinterest Summer 2026 report shows 'Formula 1 aesthetic outfit' +483%, 'Brazil jersey outfit women' +302% and 'baddie tracksuit outfit' +276%, all growth rates on undisclosed absolute bases, on a female-skewing search-and-save index rather than purchase data. The cross-dataset auditor's instruction was explicit: preserve the general sport-as-fashion finding and DISCARD the basketball-specific inference. _(A05-S4, A05-S1)_
- [PATTERN] PATTERN: the evidence base is one country. Roughly 48% of surviving signals are US-primary and closer to 70% once US-derived 'Global' signals are attributed. Europe is the primary market of zero signals here, Latin America of none; A02-S9 (Australia) is the only registry-grade non-US evidence and it measures PARTICIPATION, not fan merchandise. Greater China is excluded at launch by the brief's own reasoning (GC -13% currency-neutral in FY26, apparel units -8%, Topsports ceasing Nike online sales by January 2027, and not one retrieved Chinese price in the base). _(A02-S9, A02-S2, A04-S2, A02-S7)_

**What the machine believes**
- The demand pool is real and the fixture premise is dead, so what remains of OPP-07 is a BLOCK-AND-PROPORTION input - a women's high-rise, untapered, jersey-tucking block - routed into programmes Nike is already funding (Clark, A'One, Sabrina, Rebel Edition), not a new franchise. This is also where the cross-dataset auditor sent the analogous residual of the rejected A01-O2. _(basis: The one claim the red team never attacked is that none of the incumbent Nike women's fan shorts - Legends Flow Mesh, On-Court Victory, Logowoman Crossover, Rebel Fanwear, Sabrina - is built on a high-rise jersey-tucking women's block, while every other pillar of the brief (fixture, price, novelty) was falsified. All three orchestrator lenses and the challenger converged on the same de-scoped shape.; confidence Medium)_
- The USD 65 core / USD 75 drop rung should not be carried forward at all. It should be costed to survive at USD 50-55, and no price should be treated as a recommendation until Nike's internal list-vs-realised ASP and markdown rate by door are pulled. _(basis: The rung's only support was a comparison-set argument that the fan wall realises higher prices; the fan wall discounts 25-45% with codes, the same or worse than the USD 42.97-from-USD-65 Sabrina markdown the brief itself calls its most important price fact. Three mutually incompatible Nike price ladders coexist in the base and not one price was confirmed against a retrieved page (A03-S9, A04-S4, audit).; confidence High)_
- The two decisive tests are free and internal, and they are BETTER instruments than the ones the brief proposed: (1) Rebel Fanwear short and Caitlin Clark short weekly sell-through by door and by size, full-year FY26 rather than a snapshot, plus jersey-plus-bottom basket analysis; (2) bottoms as a share of women's basketball fan merchandise units. The brief's proposed instrument - splitting the Unrivaled Philadelphia USD 400,000 night by category - is n=1 at a privately-held two-season league to whose category receipts Nike has no stated contractual right. _(basis: Rebel Fanwear (8 May 2026) is the closest live in-market test of this exact thesis, Nike owns the number, and it appears in none of seven specialist files. The challenger's validation plan and the chair's key dependency independently name the same two pulls.; confidence High)_
- The strongest single first-party commercial signal in this stack argues against the brief's central construction decision. If the volume buyer is materially cross-gender, the right product is a UNISEX fan block offered in a women's size run - which Nike already ships (Legends Relaxed Fit Fleece, Logowoman Team 13 reversible, both listed unisex) - not a women's-graded block. This fork is deliberately NOT closed anywhere in the pipeline. _(basis: Ed Stack, Dick's Q1 2026 call, first full quarter owning Foot Locker: 'boys and girls, young men and women are buying that product' (A04-S5). The brief places this in what_we_still_dont_know while simultaneously building the whole product on a women's-specific block. Recorded as portfolio disagreement D-09.; confidence Medium)_
- The jersey-outfit-implies-a-bottom inference is the load-bearing hypothesis of the entire opportunity and it is unobserved. The competing reading - that this is a general athletic-shorts fashion cycle in which the buyer pairs the jersey with any short she likes and a jersey-matched bottom earns no premium - is actively supported by the reported success of DENIM shorts and bedazzled shirts at the Indiana Fever and Golden State Valkyries, a fan-lifestyle purchase with no matching logic at all. _(basis: A05-S4 and A05-S1 read literally argue for tops; the Klarna / Sports Innovation Lab 'Rep Her' evidence the brief leans on measures merchandise AVAILABILITY and STOCK (60%+ did not buy because product was out of stock; 79% cite variety/availability/quality gaps) and is headlined on shirts, containing no bottoms-versus-tops evidence. If anything it argues for deeper buys of what already exists.; confidence Medium)_
- This is the only surviving item that sits squarely inside a named SS28 priority space (Women's Revolution) - and it does not serve Worldball Innovation at all, should exclude Greater China at launch, and serves Uniform of Youth only incidentally. It should be presented that way rather than stretched to cover spaces it does not cover. _(basis: The brief says so explicitly and the audit's geographic-bias finding supports it. Portfolio observation: only OPP-07 sits inside a named space; the two highest-confidence items (OPP-03 at 62, OPP-08 at 50) sit outside all three by their own admission.; confidence High)_
- The supply-desert first-mover window is closing or already closed. The founding '1 piece of women's merchandise for every 9 men's' statistic dates to July 2024 and is being re-quoted as current, while the fan-bottoms slot visibly filled between May 2026 and today. An SS28 delivery arrives 18-24 months after the gap was identified - as a fast-follower into its own category. _(basis: ASI Central July 2024 framing vs the 2026 Fanatics/Nike/WNBAStore assortment; Nike's own three women's signature apparel programmes plus Rebel Fanwear plus two 2026 expansion clubs plus a wave of women's-sports DTC labels are filling it in real time.; confidence Medium)_
- Cannibalisation, not market creation, is the likeliest commercial outcome if this is funded as a franchise: a new women's fan short would split demand three ways against Clark, Sabrina and Rebel Edition programmes already funded, in a +1% unit environment, and would land in the middle of a USD 60-85 rung Nike already occupies across mesh, fleece and knee-length. _(basis: A03-S9 unit growth; the Nike WNBA fan assortment at USD 60-85; the portfolio-level observation that four of eight briefs propose product against the same rail and that any two funded without an explicit adjacency plan buy the same demand twice.; confidence Medium)_
- The brief's execution spec is heavier than its evidence can carry and should not survive into any funded scope as written: two inseams x two fabric faces x XS-3X-plus-tall x a four-colour core x jersey-matched Rebel and All-Star drops x one event-exclusive colourway per Unrivaled tour stop, on a garment costed to survive at USD 55, with three separate bonding operations and a 200-230 g/m2 target that has no measured baseline anywhere. _(basis: The spec concedes nobody has established the GSM of any current Nike basketball short. Event-exclusive colourways at a two-season startup league's arena volumes are a minimum-order-quantity problem. This also contradicts A02-S7's own VERIFIED conclusion, which the brief cites approvingly: build shorts line plans for wholesale sell-through with a replenishable core rather than drops.; confidence High)_
- The 7-inch / 9-inch ladder is a designer's judgement, not an evidence-backed length decision, in either direction. Inseam direction is unresolved across the entire pipeline (D-08) and unit share by inseam appears nowhere in seven specialist files, three skeptic rounds or the audit, in any market. _(basis: A05-S8 is classified HYPOTHESIS and rests on one athlete quote plus two modest-dress stories; A01-S8, A01-S4 and A05-O1's '6-inch standard' premise were all REJECTED on sourcing; A07-S6's women-default-to-6-inch note is a manufacturing convention, not a preference.; confidence High)_

**What the human must decide**
- Whether 'the other half of a Nike jersey' is a proposition Nike wants to own as a stated design idea at all - or whether, now that the fixture premise is falsified, the residue is too small to be worth a Council slot in the one named SS28 priority space. _(creative ambition / brand context)_ — The machine can establish that the fixture is already built and stocked with three Nike shorts, and that none of them is built on a high-rise jersey-tucking block. It cannot judge whether that remaining gap is a proposition worth a brand's ambition or a proportion revision worth a line-plan footnote. That is a question about what Nike wants to be seen making, and nothing in 58 signals measures it.
- Women's-graded block versus unisex fan block in a women's size run. The pipeline deliberately left this fork open (disagreement D-09). _(product taste / organizational knowledge)_ — The single strongest first-party commercial signal in the stack (Ed Stack: 'boys and girls, young men and women') argues unisex; the brief, the challenger and two of three rankers assume women's-graded. There is no data in the base on either side, and averaging the two would produce a garment nobody specified. Only someone who has seen Nike's own fit-block architecture, pattern library and grading economics can weigh what a second block actually costs the organisation.
- Whether to spend the SS28 line slot on Women's Revolution at all, given that the machine's own top-ranked item is a de-scoped input rather than a franchise, and that the two highest-CONFIDENCE items on the board (OPP-03 at 62, OPP-08 at 50) sit outside all three priority spaces. _(strategy)_ — This is a weighting choice between newness and certainty, and the pipeline preserved rather than resolved it (D-07): on the commercial planner's weights OPP-03 wins; on the design director's, OPP-07 wins by 25 points; on the chair's, by 9.8. Anyone re-weighting toward certainty legitimately reverses the top two. The machine cannot know what the SS28 line review needs to be able to show.

The spring 2026 Piper Sandler wave exists and was never consulted, so even the current level is stale. Which reading to act on is a brand-health call held by people who know what else is being done for this consumer.
- Whether the fixture and adjacency ask - product hanging beside the jersey in a fan door, held for a full season - can actually be secured from Dick's and Foot Locker, and at what cost to other Nike asks in the same account conversation. _(organizational knowledge)_ — The machine can read that the fan fixture exists and is occupied by Nike product. It cannot know what the account team's current leverage is, what was traded to get the existing placement, or what a fixture request costs against everything else on the joint business plan. That knowledge is in the account team's head and in no dataset.
- Whether to confirm the red team's kill shots before acting on them. Every retail fact in the challenge is a search-result summary from an egress-blocked domain; the challenger says so and says the confirmation is one buyer walking one Dick's fan wall in an afternoon. _(organizational knowledge)_ — The machine cannot retrieve the pages and cannot walk the wall. It can only flag that the case for de-scoping - which is the difference between funding a franchise and funding an input - rests on evidence of the same grade the audit warned about, and that the cheapest correction is physical, not analytical.

Three specific things must NOT be carried forward if it is selected: the USD 65-75 price rung (contradicted on both walls and unanchored by the audit's own instruction), the fixture ask (the fixture is already built and already stocked with Nike product - the opportunity's own stated kill condition is met in the wrong direction), and the six-dimensional SKU matrix.
