### OPP-03 — Twenty Washes (INVEST)

**What the machine knows**
- [PATTERN] A durability failure mode - seams opening and shrinkage/opacity loss after one to a few home washes - reproduces on Nike core basketball shorts across two Icon inseams and three independent retail venues: the Walmart Icon corpus ('holes in the seams across the legs' after one wear and one wash), Dick's Icon+ 6 inch at 3.9 stars with 67% of 64 reviewers recommending, and - found by the red team while trying to kill it - the Dick's Icon 11 inch listing ('falling apart after being worn and washed one time', 'completely see through'). This is the only reproducible consumer finding in the 58-signal base, and it survived a direct venue-artifact attack. _(A01-S3, A04-S6, A01-S2)_
- [FACT] Nike Brand apparel grew 2% currency-neutral in FY2026 on units +1%, with ASP contributing about one point driven by product MIX and already partly eroded by higher discounts and channel mix. There is no unit tailwind in apparel and no demonstrated pricing power - so full-price productivity on an existing unit pool, not volume or list price, is where apparel margin can move. This is audited filing material, the strongest verified item in the product file. _(A03-S9)_
- [FACT] Distribution has swung back to wholesale: Nike Digital declined for a tenth consecutive quarter while wholesale grew ~4%. A replenishable core carrying a rack-legible spec, sold 70/30 wholesale, is the channel-correct construct; an app-exclusive or Nike-Direct-led expression is not. _(A02-S7, A04-S1)_
- [FACT] Compression worn under the short is explicitly rules-legal at any length under FIBA provided the team matches colour, and the 2025-26 NFHS change permits multiple like-coloured bottom styles - so the layered wear pattern this programme assumes is rules-safe, and a sewn-in brief liner is redundant for the layering player. Prevalence of that layering BELOW the elite level is unmeasured (the only survey found, n=512, was 88.1% endurance athletes). _(A06-S3, A06-S6)_
- [FACT] A basketball uniform traps 0.00-1.33 kg of sweat during play, over a wider range than treadmill running, and basketball's normative whole-body sweat rate is 0.95 +/- 0.42 L/h (competition sub-population 1.4-1.6 L/h). Peer-reviewed with named samples. Consequence: any durability fix that answers with added fabric mass is in direct tension with the wet-state physics of the garment, and the engineering target (sport mean vs competitive tail) is a choice, not a finding. _(A06-S2, A06-S1)_
- [FACT] The claim environment changes inside the SS28 window and it cuts both ways. The EU Empowering Consumers Directive applies from 27 September 2026, retiring generic/uncertified environmental claims across every competitor at once - and making unsubstantiated DURABILITY claims specifically sanctionable. France's environmental-cost display becomes compulsory for textiles from October 2026 with a durability coefficient (0.67-1.45) that third parties may compute and publish if the brand does not. EMEA also already carries a two-year statutory legal guarantee for conformity defects. _(A03-S5)_
- [PATTERN] Durability is not empty claim space. Nike's own DNA copy already claims it ('lightweight-yet-durable', 'built for the grind', 'stand up to even the toughest rebound battles'), reinforced-seam language runs through the mid and value tiers (UA Baseline, AND1, Russell), Decathlon already guarantees two years and publishes minimum guaranteed uses for some products, and contract-sourcing guidance treats 140-180 GSM performance mesh as holding shape after 100+ washes. The move available is to SUBSTANTIATE a claim Nike already makes, not to open a new one - a smaller prize on a larger legal surface, and the reason '20 washes' anchors low. _(A03-S5, A04-S6)_
- [FACT] Every scaled precedent for an open-ended make guarantee on machine-washed basics was retracted: L.L.Bean ended its lifetime guarantee in 2018 after policy-violating returns doubled to ~15% of returns at a cost near USD 250M, REI capped at one year in 2013, Dr Martens dropped 'For Life' in 2018; US return fraud/abuse ran ~15.14% of returns and USD 103B in 2024 against apparel return rates of 20-30%. _(A04-S6)_
- [FACT] The observable price ladder is lower and softer than this pipeline originally assumed, and every price in it is directional only - no price anywhere in the base was confirmed against a retrieved page, because every retail host was egress-blocked to the specialists and to the developer alike. Directionally: Icon listed USD 30 (seen at USD 18.97), Icon 11 inch USD 35 (USD 28.97), DNA 8 inch USD 65 marked to USD 32.50 at Foot Locker on 2026-09-03 - a 50% cut, twice the 25% depth recorded a year earlier - with New Balance's 7 inch mesh short USD 50 to USD 25 on the same shelf. All markdown observations were taken in peak end-of-summer shorts clearance. _(A04-S6, A02-S4, A04-S4)_
- [FACT] No basketball-shorts-level unit, sell-through, markdown or returns data exists anywhere in the evidence base, in any geography; no fabric GSM, BOM or supplier-change history establishes that any cost-down ever occurred; and every consumer datapoint is United States. The causal story behind the opportunity (a price freeze forced a fabric cost-down which produced the complaints) is reverse-engineered from reviews, and its first link has itself been superseded by Nike's surgical price increases through FY26 against USD 1.5B annualised tariff cost and ~120bp of FY26 gross-margin headwind. _(A04-S6, A04-S8, A02-S4)_

**What the machine believes**
- The defect is real but the business case as written is booked at the wrong level of the P&L. The 'whole business case' sentence - moving the DNA 8 inch from a 50% to a 20% markdown recovers roughly USD 19 per unit - is a RETAIL markdown on a RETAIL price inside a programme the spec itself weights 70/30 to wholesale. Nike realises wholesale price and recovers retailer markdown only through negotiated markdown allowances, margin-protection and chargebacks (partial and negotiated, not pass-through) while carrying 100% of the BOM increment, the bespoke 20-cycle test and a per-lot QA gate. We believe a meaningful share of that USD 19 accrues to Dick's and Foot Locker rather than to Nike; nobody has quoted the recovery rate. _(basis: Red-team kill attempt 1 (economics), unrebutted; trade literature on markdown allowances and chargebacks; the spec's own stated 70/30 wholesale mix; the chair adopted this as the gate condition in portfolio.json.; confidence High)_
- The '20W' badge as specified should not ship in any form. It anchors below the 100+ washes that contract sourcing already treats as normal for team mesh, it expires inside the brief's own job story (a school/AAU season is 20-30 weeks of weekly washing), and printing a number in the season EmpCo makes unsubstantiated durability claims sanctionable converts existing puffery into an implied warranty across tens of millions of units - at a moment when France will publish a regulated durability coefficient for the whole category whether Nike prints anything or not. _(basis: Red-team kill attempts 2, 3 and 6; EmpCo and France environmental-cost display dates; contract-sourcing GSM guidance. All three rankers and the chair concurred; the chair killed the badge outright.; confidence High)_
- Roughly half the diagnosis is probably not a make problem at all. 100% polyester shrinks only about 2-5% and only above ~60C water or high dryer heat, so the residual headroom a heat-set finish can buy is small and much of the reported shrinkage is plausibly a high-heat-drying artifact no construction spec can reach. A claim benched at AATCC 135 controlled conditions (usual reported cycle count: three) will not reproduce in the complainant's dryer - which would break trust with exactly the consumers it targets. The SEAM-FAILURE half of the diagnosis survives this cleanly; the shrinkage half does not. _(basis: Red-team kill attempt 4 (fabric physics) with polyester shrinkage sources and AATCC 135 reporting convention; no counter-evidence in the base.; confidence Medium)_
- The programme is probably directionally right and is unusually cheap to falsify. Every decisive test uses data Nike already owns - warranty and returns defect codes, BOM and GSM history FY23-FY26, the eight-quarter markdown and allowance file, a colourway terminal-markdown count - obtainable in two to four weeks for well under USD 25k each, against a programme that changes no silhouette, adds no SKU, opens no market and asks for no price increase. That cost asymmetry, not the strength of the diagnosis, is what earns it a place on the board; a council can approve the validation without approving the product. _(basis: Developer confidence rationale (60) and challenger adjustment (48); validation plan items 1, 2 and 7 are all internal-data pulls with published stop conditions.; confidence High)_
- The funding source named in the original thesis may not exist. Liner deletion was the synthesised funding mechanism, but nobody in seven domains costed the liner or established that the target SKUs carry one - Nike copy on the same day described DNA styles as unlined AND as 'Lined', and Nike operates a standing 'Basketball Unlined Shorts' navigation filter, so lining varies by SKU. We believe colourway rationalisation (fewer cores, carried deeper, replenishment with a guaranteed reorder window) is the honest funding route, and liner deletion is at best a conditional cost lever. _(basis: Developer's own live checks and explicit demotion of the mechanism, flagged as a material departure from the synthesis; contradictory-evidence item rated severity high.; confidence Medium)_
- Applied uniformly across both franchises at held prices, this flattens the ladder it is meant to defend. DNA's stated reason to exist above Icon is already durability; publishing one identical make standard across a USD 30 short and a USD 50-65 short leaves a mesh face and a zip pocket to carry a USD 30 delta, and removes the durability headroom a future premium expression (Aero-FIT, Sabrina, signature) would want to claim. This argues for tiered specification rather than a single published standard - a design and merchandising call the pipeline never made. _(basis: Red-team kill attempt 8 (cannibalisation), reasoned from Nike's own DNA copy and the spec's own price ladder; the developer's counter (a premium tier is not credible on a failing core) is equally unevidenced.; confidence Medium)_
- This may be the right programme addressed to the wrong council. As written it changes no silhouette, adds no length, adds no SKU, opens no market and asks for no price - it is executed by Materials, Sourcing and Quality, not by PLM. It defers Greater China (no Worldball), is explicitly men's and boys' (no Women's Revolution), and is a make standard rather than a youth assortment (no Uniform of Youth). It sits outside all three SS28 priority spaces by its own construction. The design director ranked it FIFTH for exactly this reason (cultural relevance 1, differentiation 2 on his board) while the commercial planner ranked it FIRST; that disagreement (D-02) is a weighting difference between chairs, not a factual one, and has been preserved rather than averaged. _(basis: Red-team kill attempt 11 (strategic fit), the spec's own description of itself, and recorded disagreement D-02 in portfolio.json.; confidence High)_
- The manufacturing consistency, not the idea, is the hard part - and it is the part the base cannot price. A 20-cycle protocol is roughly 7x the normal AATCC 135 run per specimen, per colourway, per size break, per production lot, enforced through tier-2 contract factories Nike does not own, on a USD 30 garment in a year carrying USD 1.5B of annualised tariff cost and ~120bp of gross-margin headwind. The spec concedes this in its own right-to-win section and offers no cost estimate. _(basis: Red-team kill attempt 9 (execution/manufacturing); AATCC 135 reporting convention; tariff and margin disclosures.; confidence Medium)_

**What the human must decide**
- Whether Nike Basketball Apparel should spend an SS28 decision cycle on line-plan productivity at all, rather than on newness. The machine can say this consumes no line slot and carries the portfolio's highest confidence (62 chair / 48 post-challenge); it cannot say whether a brand in a turnaround should give its scarce PLM attention to fixing what it already sells. _(strategy)_ — This is a portfolio-posture question about what Nike Basketball is for in SS28. The engine's three rankers split hard on it (commercial planner first, PLM second, design director fifth) and the split traces entirely to how many of 100 points a chair puts on differentiation and cultural relevance. There is no evidence that adjudicates a weighting preference - only a taste for what a season should say.
- Whether to accept the de-scoped version (silent make fix, no badge, no guarantee, funded by colourway rationalisation, price held) or to insist on a consumer-facing expression. The machine has killed the '20W' badge and the season-long guarantee on evidence; what it cannot decide is whether a fix nobody can see is worth doing at all, or whether Nike's brand only earns a return on quality it is allowed to say out loud. _(brand context)_ — The value of an unspoken quality improvement is a brand-equity judgment on a time horizon no dataset in this base covers. The one instrument that could inform it - a badged-vs-unbadged in-door A/B plus conjoint - costs USD 150-250k and a full season, and would have to be authorised by the same decision it is meant to inform.
- Whether to apply one make standard across Icon and DNA, or to tier it and preserve durability as DNA's reason to exist above Icon. The machine can state the tension (DNA already sells on durability; a uniform published standard leaves a mesh face and a zip pocket to carry a USD 30 delta) but cannot resolve it. _(product taste)_ — Resolving it requires a view on what a franchise ladder should mean to a consumer standing at a rack, and on what headroom Nike wants to reserve for Aero-FIT and signature expressions later. The base holds no unit split by franchise, inseam, channel or region - so 'the franchise that carries the units' is itself an untested assumption - and no evidence exists either way on how consumers read a shared spec badge across price rungs.
- How much of the diagnosis Nike is willing to own before knowing the answer. The machine has established that seam failure reproduces across three venues and two SKUs, and separately that shrinkage is plausibly a customer high-heat-drying artifact. Deciding whether to fix seams now on that reproduction, or to hold until returns defect codes and a GSM/BOM history come back, is a risk-appetite call. _(intuition)_ — The engine can quantify the cost of waiting (weeks, tens of thousands of dollars) but not the cost of another season of 'the worst quality product I've ever bought and worn from Nike' sitting on a Dick's page. Nobody has established a benchmark for what a normal recommend rate is on a USD 30 mesh short, so whether 3.9 stars and 67% is a crisis or category-normal is currently an impression, not a finding.
- Whether Nike wants to be the brand that publishes a durability number in a market that is about to publish one for it. France's mandated durability coefficient arrives from October 2026 and third parties may compute and publish it if the brand does not; EmpCo makes an unsubstantiated durability claim sanctionable from 27 September 2026. Getting ahead of a regulated score, matching it, or staying silent is a positioning choice with legal consequences. _(brand context)_ — This is a claims-posture decision across 27 jurisdictions that trades reputational leadership against implied-warranty exposure on tens of millions of units. It requires Nike Global Legal, EMEA Regulatory Affairs and a brand view on how Nike wants to be seen when the coefficient publishes - none of which is an evidence question, and the review itself is time-critical at roughly three weeks out.
- Whether Nike's wholesale partners will co-operate rather than pocket the benefit. The machine has shown the recovery is booked at retail level in a wholesale-weighted programme; the human must decide whether to open the markdown-allowance conversation with Dick's and Foot Locker at all, and on what terms - and whether partners will honour or resent administering any make promise. _(organizational knowledge)_ — Trade terms, allowance recovery rates and account relationship history are first-party commercial knowledge held inside Nike NA Wholesale Finance and account management. None of it exists in the evidence base, and no public source can substitute for what a merchant knows about how a specific partner behaves.
- Whether a 20-plus-cycle seam and dimensional-stability spec can actually be enforced through tier-2 factories Nike does not own, and at what cost - and therefore whether Sourcing and Quality can carry this in the same year as USD 1.5B of annualised tariff cost. If not, the badge question is moot and so is the programme. _(organizational knowledge)_ — Factory capability, per-lot QA cost, and Sourcing's appetite in this specific year are internal operational facts the engine has no access to. The spec itself concedes that consistency, not the idea, is the moat, and offers no cost estimate for it.
- Which market leads, and whether deferring Greater China is acceptable. The spec leads US, then UK/Germany/France, then Japan/Australia, and defers GC explicitly on marketplace grounds (apparel units -8%, revenue -13% cn, Topsports stopping online sales by January 2027). SS28 priorities point at Greater China. _(strategy)_ — Every consumer datapoint in this base is United States; EMEA, Nike's second geography, has not one signal in which it is the primary market, and there is no Chinese price or sell-through datum anywhere in the base. Choosing a lead market against SS28 stated priority is a strategic bet the evidence cannot arbitrate.

**If selected:** If the PLM / Design team selects OPP-03, the first and only funded step is their call to commission the two-to-three-week internal gate before any product work begins: re-model the recovery at Nike REALISED wholesale revenue with the actual markdown-allowance and chargeback rates for Icon and DNA by partner over eight quarters, run in parallel with the FY24-FY26 returns/warranty defect-code pull and the FY23-FY26 GSM and BOM history - with the stop condition published in advance (no realised-revenue multiple over incremental cost, no defect-code elevation against the Nike apparel benchmark, or no specification drift and no bench failure means the programme stops there).

_Do not brief this, develop concepts, commission artwork, or place it in an SS28 line review on the strength of this gate. Three things in it are not established and one is actively wrong as written: nobody has shown that any fabric GSM or construction cost-down ever occurred (the entire causal story is reverse-engineered from consumer reviews and may simply be false); nobody has counted or costed the sewn-in liner that the original thesis nominated as the funding source, and it may not exist on the target SKUs; there is no benchmark anywhere in the base for what a normal review score is on a USD 30 mesh short, so 'weak quality perception' is an impression rather than a measurement; and the USD 19-per-unit recovery that the spec itself calls 'the whole business case' is a retail markdown booked into a 70/30 wholesale programme, so an unknown and probably minority share of it is Nike's. The '20W' badge and the season-long make guarantee are both killed and must not be carried forward in any deck - printing a number below the 100+ washes contract sourcing treats as normal, in the season EmpCo makes unsubstantiated durability claims sanctionable, converts existing puffery into an implied warranty across tens of millions of units. Preserved disagreement that must travel with any onward decision (D-02): the commercial planner ranked this FIRST and the design director ranked it FIFTH, because it builds no identity, recruits no athlete, tells no story a consumer repeats, and sits outside all three SS28 priority spaces by its own admission; that is a weighting difference between chairs and has not been averaged away. Nothing here has been validated against Nike first-party commercial data, because none exists anywhere in this pipeline._

### OPP-02 — Found Outdoors (INVEST)

**What the machine knows**
- [FACT] Nike already ships the garment this opportunity proposes to create. The DNA Men's Dri-FIT 6" UV Woven (FN2659) carries UVA/UVB protection, side pockets, a phone-sized zip pocket and a rebound-durability claim, and is merchandised on Nike AU, IN, MY, ID and JP and at Rebel Sport, Hibbett and Dick's. Three research domains independently wrote those same features up as unowned white space from the same un-run catalogue query. This is capture and findability, not invention - which shrinks the prize from a new occasion to trade-up. _(A03-S7, A06-S4, A07-S8, A02-S7)_
- [PATTERN] Heat load in outdoor basketball is corroborated by three evidence pools that share no source: peer-reviewed physiology measuring 0.00-1.33 kg of sweat trapped in a basketball uniform and a 0.95 +/- 0.42 L/h whole-body sweating rate (A06-S2, VERIFIED); documented institutional behaviour change, with Philippine athletic meets moved off the 9am-3pm window from 2024 after one provincial meet recorded more heat-related than sports-related injuries and Gurgaon court surfaces above 50C (A06-S5); and a competitor's multi-season commercial platform in Li-Ning's Wade UPF 50+ / AT Dry line, running consistently Spring 2023 through 2025 (A03-S7). This is PAT-11 and it is the strongest cross-domain corroboration in the whole evidence base. _(A06-S2, A06-S5, A03-S7, A03-S4, A01-S7)_
- [FACT] The proposed moat is not a first. AATCC Test Method 183 already provides for measuring UV transmittance with specimens in either the dry OR WET status, and ASTM D6603 already conditions labelled specimens (40 launderings plus simulated solar exposure) and explicitly documents that stretching fabric decreases UPF by increasing optical porosity. Coolibar already markets 'blocks 98% of UVA/UVB rays - wet or dry'. 'UPF 50+ certified wet and stretched' is therefore a purchasable, off-the-shelf test election that Li-Ning or Anta can answer in one test cycle - a basketball-category merchandising first, not a defensible asset. _(A06-S7, A03-S7)_
- [FACT] The shelves the brief itself names contradict the price. Foot Locker shows Nike Dri-FIT DNA 8" marked from USD 65.00 to USD 32.50 (50% off, twice the 25% the spec used as its empirical ceiling) and DNA 6" from USD 50.00 to USD 37.50. Rebel Sport - the named lead door in the named best-evidenced lead market - lists the exact UV Woven SKU at AUD 44.99 against an AUD 75-80 ask. USD 55 is a 47% step and AUD 75-80 a 67-78% step over what the same garment transacts at on the same rack. _(A04-S6, A02-S4, A04-S4)_
- [FACT] The full feature composition is already commoditised at private-label price. NORTHYARD - an Amazon private label already named in the marketplace file - ships UPF 50+, a 5/7/9 inch inseam ladder (plus a 10/7/5 variant), unlined construction, quick-dry, four-way stretch, zip pockets and reflective strips in one SKU with 'Basketball' in the title, ranking in Amazon Best Sellers for Men's Athletic Shorts. The composition A07-S8 called unowned has been answered by a brand with no design team. _(A07-S8, A02-S4)_
- [FACT] The channel logic is verified and unambiguous: Nike wholesale grew in both Q4 and full-year FY26 while Nike Digital declined for a tenth consecutive quarter, and performance basketball is one of Nike's few growth engines. A rack-legible outdoor short with no product copy to read is a wholesale product, and Nike already owns rack space at every door this franchise needs - Dick's, Foot Locker, Hibbett, Rebel, JD AU, Titan 22. _(A02-S7, A04-S1)_
- [FACT] Nike has already made and marketed this exact consumer argument one category over: the S.T. Flare, released June 2025 as Nike's first China-only performance basketball shoe, explicitly built after studying Chinese outdoor courts for durability, traction and heat. It launched at approximately RMB 899 (USD 125) - premium, not value - so the same signal that supports the strategic precedent argues against the RMB 279-299 value-tier recommendation. _(A01-S7)_
- [FACT] The lead market named by the SS28 priority space is a contracting branded segment for Nike. Greater China apparel units fell 8% in FY26 and Q4 FY26 GC revenue fell 12% reported / 17% currency-neutral to USD 1.30B; adidas beat Nike in Tmall 618 2026. There is not one retrieved Chinese price or sell-through datum anywhere in the base, and the file holds an unreconciled contradiction on whether Li-Ning basketball is falling (-19%, 2025) or recovering (+5%, H1 2026) - same company, adjacent periods, opposite direction, both VERIFIED. _(A04-S2, A02-S2, A02-S3, A04-S11)_
- [FACT] Two execution constraints are established and were not in the brief. ARPANSA grants the UPF Certification Trade Mark only where a sample of the same type, quality AND COLOUR has been tested, and pale shades rate lowest - which makes per-colourway certification economically incompatible with the seasonal per-market local-graphic strategy the same brief proposes (the core palette includes 'stone'). Separately, Nike defines Dri-FIT UV at platform level as 'minimum UPF 30' and prints no numeric UPF and no certification mark on FN2659 in any market including Australia, so printing a number is a global claims-policy reversal across the whole Dri-FIT UV range, not a hangtag change - on an 86% polyester / 14% spandex elastic woven, the substrate most exposed to the stretch effect. _(A06-S7, A03-S5)_
- [PATTERN] Scalability is the highest on the board and is not contested by anyone. This is the only candidate that is genuinely multi-region and multi-season on day one - GC, APLA, the Gulf, the US Sun Belt and Australia - on a garment already in the doors it needs, with essentially zero incremental inventory liability. All three orchestrator lenses scored it 5 and the red team conceded execution risk is unusually low. _(A02-S1, A02-S7, A04-S1)_

**What the machine believes**
- The binding constraint is findability, not function - i.e. the reason seven researchers with a live catalogue could not find FN2659 is the same reason a consumer at a Foot Locker rack cannot, and naming plus a legible spec block is worth more than any feature added to the garment. _(basis: Inference from a real observation (four independent domains missed a shipping SKU; A02-S7 verifies the channel has swung to wholesale where there is no PDP; A07-S9 shows Li-Ning, BadFive and ballaholic print function and place on the outside of the garment while Nike speaks tonal minimalism). Nobody has measured rack legibility or search behaviour anywhere in the base. This is the load-bearing assumption of the entire de-scoped programme and it is a HYPOTHESIS.; confidence Medium)_
- The certification programme should not be funded as a moat. Its residual value is marketing legibility inside basketball, not physical protection or exclusivity - and the underlying physics may already favour the incumbent fabric. _(basis: AATCC 183 and ASTM D6603 remove primacy; peer-reviewed testing of 34 polyester sportswear fabrics (Aguilera et al. 2023) found over 75% already rate UPF 40-50+ untreated and that moisture SIGNIFICANTLY INCREASED protection factors by over 20% - the opposite of the thesis that spawned the feature. The genuinely open variable narrows to biaxial thigh strain, which ASTM already discusses. All three portfolio rankers and the challenger converged on refusing the certification.; confidence High)_
- The USD 55 / AUD 75-80 price step does not exist and pursuing it would convert this from a productivity move into a margin risk. At best the franchise holds current band and earns its return on units and full-price sell-through rather than ASP. _(basis: Live retrievals of the realised prices on the same garment in the same doors; the audit's finding that no price in the base is anchored to a retrieved page and three incompatible Nike ladders coexist; the observable clearing band of USD 29-69; syndicated (low-rigour, directional only) research that UPF garments already carry a 25-40% premium with 41% of buyers citing cost as the barrier and ~42% not knowing what UPF means.; confidence High)_
- UV is the legible, certifiable expression of a heat need rather than the need itself, and the primary use occasion may not be a sunny one. If everyday play has genuinely moved to dawn and dusk in the priority markets, dry-time, low wet cling, fabric weight and night visibility outrank UPF, and UPF matters mainly for multi-hour weekend tournaments. _(basis: A06-S5 documents the dawn/dusk shift in Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Gurgaon, the UAE and the Philippines; open sun-protection literature retrieved by the challenger states pickup games 'often take place between 10am and 4pm'. The base and the open literature disagree and the disagreement is preserved, not averaged. Compounding it: melanoma epidemiology puts the trunk at ~45.1% of male cases and the thigh - the one region a short already covers - is neither the highest-exposure nor the highest-risk site for a male 15-35 target, while A06-S7 itself records UPF sleeves as culturally accepted and UPF shorts as not.; confidence Medium)_
- This is a franchise EXTENSION that replaces rather than adds unless the ladder is planned explicitly against the DNA 6". A named 9" hero five dollars above an incumbent carrying the same UV, pocket and durability claims most likely produces a split buy, not a trade-up. _(basis: The brief concedes the prize is trade-up and findability; Nike apparel growth is already price-led with units +1% (A03-S9, VERIFIED) and GC apparel units -8% (A04-S2, VERIFIED), which is the pattern that produced the current markdown depth. No inseam sell-through split by door type exists anywhere in the base, in any market.; confidence Medium)_
- Australia is the better proof market than Greater China for SS28, even though SS28 priority points at GC - highest UPF literacy, the standard the claim is written against, and the best-evidenced market in the file - but Australia's read may not generalise to where the volume actually is. _(basis: A02-S9 (VERIFIED) and A06-S7 on Australian UPF literacy and the ARPANSA scheme; against it, Australia has roughly 800 courts against China's 1.1M+, an indoor-club orientation, an inverted season, no Nike basketball rights (iAthletic for the Boomers and Opals, Champion for the NBL), and the trade press states directly that Australia is no test market. Recorded as unresolved in the portfolio, not settled here.; confidence Low)_
- The most valuable free action attached to this opportunity is the eight-quarter Nike AU sell-through pull by inseam, gender, price and door from Rebel (~163 doors), JD AU and Foot Locker AU that the portfolio folded in from OPP-04. It returns the dataset an Australia-first launch programme would have taken eighteen months to produce, this quarter, at no cost and no inventory risk. _(basis: Chair resolution D-06: all three rankers agreed the OPP-04 proving-ground mechanism is arithmetically void because the SS28 buy closes around the month an Australian range would land, and all three agreed the pull is the right residual action. Whether it happens now depends on an owner being named.; confidence High)_
- There is no demand evidence that anyone pays a premium for an outdoor basketball short - for Nike, Li-Ning, Anta or anyone. The entire demand case is inferred from participation, physiology and a competitor's assortment decision. _(basis: The developer's own confidence rationale and the challenger both state it explicitly: zero sell-through, zero conversion, zero search-volume and zero consumer-research evidence in 58 signals. The nearest proxy category - all sun-protective clothing, every garment type, every sport - is sized at roughly USD 1.4B by 2030 by syndicated research, immaterial against Nike apparel at USD 13.4B; treat that sizing as directional only.; confidence High)_

**What the human must decide**
- Is 'make what we already ship findable' a legitimate use of an SS28 line-review slot and the Worldball Innovation narrative - or is it line-plan housekeeping that should happen anyway and be funded from assortment, with the innovation budget spent on something that creates newness? _(strategy / creative ambition)_ — The engine can establish that the productivity return is high and the incremental inventory liability near zero, and that the newness is near zero (differentiation 2, whitespace 2). It cannot decide what a season is FOR. Whether SS28 is a year to compound distribution on an existing block or a year that must produce a story is a chair's judgement about the brand's momentum, and the three orchestrator lenses split on exactly this - the PLM director and commercial planner voted INVEST, the design director voted EXPLORE because the challenger removed the only thing making it a franchise rather than a fix (D-05).
- What does this franchise get called, and does Nike have a name worth spending? The brief's heritage route is a factual error - 'Blacktop' was Reebok's 1991 streetball line; Nike's outdoor lineage is Air Raid, Air Raid II, Air Darwin and Ndestrukt, all footwear and all unproven as apparel franchise names. The fallback, 'Nike DNA Outdoor', inherits shelf space but no meaning. _(brand context / product taste / organizational knowledge)_ — Naming is the entire mechanism of this opportunity - if findability is the constraint, the name IS the product decision - and it is the one thing no dataset can produce. The machine can rule the Reebok mark out and confirm what the Nike archive holds; it cannot judge whether Air Raid can carry apparel, whether Nike Basketball wants to spend a heritage asset here, or what a name has to feel like on a rack in Manila. Trademark clearance and archive equity also live in organisational knowledge the engine has no access to.
- Lead market: Greater China as the SS28 scale bet, or Australia and the Philippines as proof markets first? SS28 priority points at GC; the evidence base holds not one Chinese price or sell-through datum, an unreconciled Li-Ning -19%/+5% contradiction, GC apparel units -8% and a market where adidas is winning on locally created product. _(strategy / organizational knowledge)_ — The evidence genuinely points both ways and the audit forbade averaging - a value entry tier and a premium durability story need different products, different margins and different channels. The decisive inputs are internal and organisational: whether Greater China has the local creation and sourcing capability standing today to run the adidas mechanism rather than a translated global line, and whether the region's leadership will carry a franchise into a contracting segment. Neither is in any dataset the engine can reach.
- Price posture: hold at or near the current band (approximately USD 45-50 / AUD 45-55 / PHP 1,995) and earn the return on units and full-price sell-through, or attempt a step and accept the markdown risk the live shelves already demonstrate? _(strategy / organizational knowledge)_ — The engine has established what the garment transacts at today and that no price in the base is anchored to sell-through. It cannot see Nike's list-versus-realised ASP, markdown allowances by partner, tariff absorption or margin box, and it cannot weigh what holding price signals to wholesale partners in a marketplace that turned promotional in summer 2026. That is a commercial judgement made with first-party data the engine has none of.
- Does the wet-and-stretched certification get funded at all - and if so, as a moat, as a marketing asset, or as an option exercised only if a market proves someone pays for it? _(strategy / brand context)_ — The engine can show the claim is a purchasable test election and that ARPANSA's per-colour rule collides with the local-graphic strategy. It cannot decide whether Nike wants to be the brand that publishes numbers in this category, which is a positioning choice with spillover across the whole Dri-FIT UV platform, nor whether Legal will reverse a standing global posture of not printing a UPF rating. That gate is an internal legal and brand-governance call, and it is time-pressured by the EU Empowering Consumers Directive applying 27 September 2026.
- Inseam architecture: is the 9" a knee-clearing outdoor performance length or a lifestyle coverage length, and does the ladder go 5/7/9 as proposed while the existing block runs 6/8/10/11 with the LONGEST inseam at the LOWEST price? _(product taste / organizational knowledge)_ — The base contains no unit share by inseam in any market - the auditor flagged this as absent from seven specialist files, three skeptic rounds and the audit, and the specialists contradict each other on direction (A07-S4 argues the poles, A02-S5's own source says 7-9 inches, Nike's live ladder is continuous). Fit-block proportion and where a hem sits in a low defensive stance are design judgements made on a body, not in a dataset.
- Who owns this, and does the organisation fund the cheap half? The programme only works if it is booked against the SS28 assortment as a naming, laddering and legibility action - if it is handed to a development budget, Nike ends up paying per-colourway test cost for a feature a private label already ships at a price the shelf has already refused. _(organizational knowledge)_ — Ownership, budget line and the discipline to keep a de-scoped programme de-scoped are organisational facts. The engine has watched three specialist domains independently propose a product Nike already ships; it has no visibility into which function would take this on or whether a merchandising action survives contact with a development calendar. This is the portfolio's stated key dependency for OPP-02.
- Is the sun story on the wrong garment? If the high-exposure zones in basketball are the ones clothing does not reach and UPF sleeves are already culturally accepted while UPF shorts are not, the category-correct UPF hero may be a top or sleeve Nike already sells. _(product taste / brand context)_ — The engine can lay out the epidemiology, the exposure zones and A06-S7's own note on cultural acceptance. It cannot decide what a basketball consumer will read as credible or as try-hard on a leg versus an arm, or whether Nike Basketball wants a sun story at all. That is taste, and it is exactly the judgement the design chair was spawned to make and did not resolve.

**If selected:** If the human PLM / Design team selects OPP-02, their call would be to commission the de-scoped programme only - name and ladder FN2659 (add a knee-clearing 9" and a boys' 5", extend the women's block, build the COURT RATED legibility system, hold price) against the SS28 assortment rather than a development budget, with the two free reads run first: Nike's list-versus-realised ASP and markdown by SKU, inseam and region for eight quarters, and the eight-quarter Nike AU sell-through pull from Rebel, JD AU and Foot Locker AU that OPP-04 was folded into.

_DO NOT PROCEED. No product briefing, concept development, fit-block work, certification testing, naming exploration or supplier engagement may begin on OPP-02 until a human PLM / Design decision-maker has selected it. This gate is a decision package, not an approval: the opportunity carries a chair composite of 55.5 and a red-team-adjusted confidence of 40, down from 62, with three of its load-bearing assertions - the certification moat, the price step and the feature-composition novelty - broken by live retrieval. It survives only in the de-scoped form above, and every price and every inseam in this file is unanchored to first-party data. The three named non-funded items - the wet-and-stretched certification programme, the USD 55 / AUD 75-80 price rung and per-colourway test election - must not be reinstated by implication if this is selected._

### OPP-08 — Full Range (EXPLORE)

**What the machine knows**
- [FACT] Nike's live US basketball shorts ladder runs from a DNA 6-inch at USD 65 down to a DNA Academy 11-inch at USD 37, with a DNA 8-inch at USD 55 and a DNA 10-inch at USD 50 in between - so within the premium DNA franchise, longer lengths do list cheaper, and a USD 50-55 longer-length rung already exists. _(A02-S4, A02-S5, A04-S6)_
- [FACT] In the largest big-and-tall door checked (Kohl's), Nike's entire Big & Tall basketball shorts assortment consists of exactly two franchises - DNA Academy 11-inch and Dri-FIT Icon 11-inch - both of which are Nike's cheapest makes. Nike offers no premium-make basketball short in extended sizes in that door. Both are 11-inch, so the extended-size offer there is length-appropriate and make-inappropriate. _(A02-S4, A02-S5, A04-S6)_
- [FACT] The Dri-FIT Icon franchise - one of those two extended-size options - carries a reproducible durability complaint corpus: 3.9 stars and 67% recommending across 64 reviews at Dick's, plus 'paper-thin', see-through and holes-in-seams-after-one-wash complaints in the Walmart corpus. The same complaint reproduced on a different SKU at a third retailer under OPP-03's red team. _(A04-S6, A01-S3)_
- [FACT] Nothing in this length band transacts at list. The Big & Tall DNA Academy 11-inch is selling at USD 27.75 against USD 37 at Kohl's (25% off) and Nike DNA shorts at USD 48.75 against USD 65 at Foot Locker (25% off), with the DNA 10-inch previously observed near 38% off. Both ends of the ladder are promotional; the long band is the most discounted band in the category. _(A02-S4, A04-S6, A04-S4)_
- [FACT] The US headline 'inversion' does not reproduce in the UK, a market the brief never checked. At constant length, Nike DNA (~8 in) is GBP 64.99 against DNA Academy (~8 in) at GBP 44.99 - a GBP 20 franchise premium - while at constant franchise, Academy 8-inch GBP 44.99 against Academy 11-inch GBP 32.99 is a GBP 12 length effect. Roughly two-thirds of the gap is franchise tiering, not inseam. _(A02-S4, A02-S5)_
- [FACT] The channel this product needs is the channel Nike is currently winning in: Nike wholesale grew 4% in both Q4 and full-year FY26 while Nike Digital declined for a tenth consecutive quarter. Extended-size and long-inseam volume sits in wholesale and extended-size doors (Kohl's, Dick's, Academy, Hibbett, Amazon, DXL). _(A02-S7)_
- [FACT] Mix, not units, is the only available growth lever: Nike Brand apparel reached USD 13.4B in FY26 on units +1%, with ASP contributing about 1 point drawn from mix and already partially eroded by higher discounts. Any margin from this idea has to come from moving units up the ladder, not from category growth. _(A03-S9)_
- [FACT] A dated, actionable rules opening exists: NFHS Rule 3-4-5 (2025-26) permits multiple styles of like-coloured uniform bottoms among teammates, explicitly including for religious and personal accommodation, which makes a graded long bottom legal on a US high-school roster alongside a standard game short. FIBA separately requires shorts to end at or above the knee with colour-matched compression. _(A06-S3)_
- [FACT] Nike's own women's bottoms sizing guidance instructs buyers whose waist and hip fall in different sizes to order by hip measurement - which loads waist fit onto a drawcord. This is documented Nike guidance, but it is generic industry-standard bottoms boilerplate, not a basketball-specific fit finding. _(A06-S9)_
- [PATTERN] A value competitor holds the long-and-extended space at a price Nike cannot approach: AND1 All Court 11-inch to 5XL at USD 9.98 at Walmart, alongside Amazon multipack behaviour (Amazon Essentials 2-pack USD 7.97), with one anonymous reviewer describing AND1 as 'affordable and cultural' versus Nike or adidas. The strength of the pattern is the price and size availability; the motive attributed to the buyer is not established. _(A01-S9, A02-S4)_
- [PATTERN] The inseam direction of the category is genuinely unresolved inside this evidence base and is NOT averaged away here: A07-S4 argues proportion has split to the poles and Nike should abandon the 9-10 inch middle; A02-S5's own cited source (Under Armour Playbook) says modern performance runs 7-9 inches; A05-S3's Hibbett source says retro runs 9 inches or longer; and Nike's live ladder runs 6-11 inches continuously with pockets at every length. The cross-dataset audit's verdict is that no one in the base holds a single unit of sell-through by inseam - the churn itself is the finding. _(A07-S4, A02-S5, A05-S3, A05-S9)_
- [FACT] The exact load-bearing distribution decision in this brief - full size run, all styles, price parity, integrated on the floor in physical doors - has a documented public failure precedent. Old Navy BODEQUALITY launched nationally in August 2021 and by May 2022 extended sizes were pulled from roughly 75 US and 15 Canadian stores, with Gap Inc.'s CEO citing overestimated in-store demand, too-broad a launch and over-planned larger sizes creating excess inventory. Price parity itself survived; the door-level physical size run did not. _(A02-S7, A04-S4)_

**What the machine believes**
- The honest surviving claim is narrower than the brief's headline. It is not 'Nike prices coverage as cheapness'; it is 'Nike offers no premium make in extended sizes, and its two cheapest franchises - one of them carrying a seam-failure review corpus - are the only ones a 3XL player can buy in the biggest big-and-tall door.' _(basis: Red-team reframing after the UK retrieval decomposed the headline gap into a GBP 20 franchise effect and a GBP 12 length effect, leaving the size-and-make observation intact and unbroken while the length-and-price architecture claim shrank to roughly a third of its stated size.; confidence High)_

**What the human must decide**
- Is size inclusion at premium make a brand position Nike takes because it is right, or an inventory bet Nike takes because it pays? The machine can price the trade-up and it can show that the identical proposition (full size run, price parity, integrated physical merchandising) was retrenched at Old Navy within nine months - but it cannot tell you whether Nike should carry a knowingly margin-dilutive flat MSRP across extended sizes as a statement of who the brand is for. _(brand context)_ — This is a values-and-positioning call with a known cost and no ROI proof on either side. The evidence base contains a documented commercial failure of the exact mechanism and no counter-case of it succeeding; a decision to do it anyway is a deliberate brand investment, and only a human owner of Nike's brand meaning can authorise spending margin on meaning.
- Is the DNA Academy price point a defect or a deliberate weapon? The machine has established that Nike's only extended-size basketball shorts in the largest big-and-tall door are its two cheapest franchises. It cannot tell you whether that is neglect to be corrected or an intentional opening-price defence against AND1 and private label in that door - and the same facts support both readings. _(organizational knowledge)_ — The answer lives in Nike's internal franchise-role definitions, account-level price architecture and the intent behind the Academy sub-brand. None of that is in any of 58 signals, and no public retrieval can distinguish an intended role from an unintended outcome.

- Does the narrower surviving claim - 'no premium make in extended sizes' - deserve an SS28 line slot at all, or is it a merchandising instruction that should be issued to the price file and the size curve without a brief? The challenger's strongest counterargument is that a PLM could put an 11-inch into DNA next season for the cost of a line-plan meeting. _(strategy)_ — This is a question about how Nike's own organisation allocates line slots, development budget and merchant attention, and about whether a fix routed through merchandising actually gets executed or quietly dies. The machine has no visibility into which route delivers inside this company.
- Is 'better made, correctly priced, no athlete, no collab, no drop' a proposition Nike can sell at USD 55 in this category? - Is the coverage-first and modest-dressing consumer a population Nike wants to serve on the performance wall regardless of measured size, given nine years in which Nike's live modest collection never added a long basketball bottom? The rules opening (NFHS 3-4-5) is real, dated and actionable; the demand behind it is a decade-stale hypothesis. _(brand context)_ — Nobody has sized this segment in any market, and the evidence is three qualitative items, two from 2014-2017. Serving it may be right for reasons that do not appear in a sell-through model, and that trade-off is not one an evidence engine is entitled to make.

The machine can specify the ask; only humans can find out whether buyers will hold it.
- Does an opportunity that explicitly deprioritises Greater China and leads with the US belong in an SS28 line whose named priority space is Worldball? The machine records that the price anomaly does not reproduce in the UK and that GC is promotional across the segment - but the priority spaces were given as context, not constraints. _(strategy)_ — How hard SS28's stated priority spaces bind, and what it costs politically and commercially to fund a US-led architecture move against them, is organisational and strategic knowledge held by the PLM leadership team, not by the evidence.

**If selected:** If the human PLM / Design team selects OPP-08, the human's call is to authorise the cheapest kill test on the board first - a two-week internal price-file decomposition separating franchise effect from length effect at constant length and constant franchise across US and UK, followed by one 11-inch listed inside the premium DNA franchise at USD 50-55 for a single season in existing fabric, held on nike.com and one wholesale door against a control door - and to decide only after that read whether the size-and-make brief returns for development.

### OPP-04 — Southern Court (WATCH)

**What the machine knows**
- [FACT] Australian basketball participation is registry-scale and independently corroborated on two different instruments: roughly 1.3M players (second among team sports) with 450,000+ women and girls, alongside NBL 2025-26 attendance of 1,231,796, +9%, 63 sell-outs and a third consecutive million-plus season. The audit's only correction to the attendance figure was that it had been UNDERSTATED, and the NBL27 dates (19 Sep 2026 to 14 Feb 2027) verify exactly. This is the highest-verification non-US material in the 58-signal base. _(A02-S9, A05-S6)_
- [FACT] The competitive shelf in performance basketball is retreating, on VERIFIED corporate disclosure: adidas basketball -21% in the quarter, Under Armour's whole basketball business guided at USD 100-120M with Curry apparel available only through October 2026, Puma basketball a residual. The NBL's own on-court apparel partner is Champion, whose Australian shorts wall tops out at AUD 61.95 - below Nike's existing UPF short. New Balance (+19% to USD 9.2B, apparel past USD 1B, 80 new doors, already at the 7-inch inseam in Foot Locker) is the counter-moving exception that dates the window. _(A04-S3, A02-S8, A02-S9)_
- [FACT] Nike already ships the garment this brief proposes to create, into the exact Australian doors it names. The DNA 6-inch UV Woven (FN2659) carries UVA/UVB protection, side pockets, a phone-secure zip pocket and an abrasion claim, and is stocked at Rebel (~163 stores) at AUD 69.99 - the same price the brief recommends for its new core. Nike also runs a continuous 6/8/10/11-inch DNA ladder through Rebel, JD Sports AU (68 stores) and Foot Locker AU, and the DNA 8-inch is discounted to AUD 34.99 from AUD 59.99 on that same rack. Four specialist domains independently declared this a white space, which measures a capture failure rather than a gap. _(A03-S7, A02-S4, A02-S7, A04-S6)_
- [FACT] The proposed differentiator - UPF certified in both dry-unstretched and wet-stretched states - is not a first. AS/NZS 4399 rates dry unstretched fabric and requires the label warning about wet and stretched performance; wet/stretched testing is a known optional laboratory protocol, and Australian brands already market the claim (Sheila: UPF 50+ 'wet or dry'; Sun2Sea: 50+ UPF 'WetnDry'). Separately, the audit downgraded the underlying UV signal on two grounds: concrete/asphalt albedo of 2-15% is among the LOWEST of outdoor surfaces, and untreated 100% polyester technical sportswear already tests UPF 40-50+ dry. _(A06-S7, A03-S7)_
- [FACT] Nike holds no Australian basketball rights position. Champion holds the NBL on-court contract through NBL26-27; iAthletic has supplied Basketball Australia's Boomers, Opals, Rollers, Gliders and junior teams for over five years and launched new national-team uniforms in August 2026; Foot Locker - a retailer, not Nike - holds a major Boomers sponsorship. The brief's women's-colourway / She Hoops platform is therefore not merely unevidenced, it is occupied by incumbents. _(A02-S9, A04-S3)_
- [FACT] There is no shorts commercial data for Australia - or for any geography - anywhere in this base: not one unit, sell-through, realised price or markdown rate. The AUD prices in the brief are search summaries; Rebel Sport and ARPANSA pages were both egress-blocked. The cross-dataset audit is explicit that not one price in the whole base was confirmed against a retrieved page and that three mutually incompatible Nike ladders coexist. Consequently the Australian shorts pool cannot be sized at all - AUD 5M and AUD 50M are both consistent with what is known. _(A02-S1, A02-S4, A03-S9)_
- [PATTERN] Across the pipeline the systemic pattern is that specialists propose product Nike already ships, and OPP-04 is an instance of it: the same FN2659 SKU closed independently declared white spaces in three other briefs. The pattern's practical consequence here is that the Australian ask is cheaper than written (live inventory, live doors) and newer-sounding than it is (a hangtag, a naming and an inseam extension on a shipped garment). _(A03-S7, A06-S4, A02-S4)_
- [PATTERN] Nike's apparel pricing environment does not support the AUD 79.99 step: apparel grew 2% currency-neutral on units +1% with the ASP gain coming from mix and already partly eroded by discounts, the US marketplace turned increasingly promotional with elevated markdowns cited, and the premium shorts tier is observed clearing only at 25-50% off. The nearest full-price competitor to the proposed rung is Nike's own marked-down DNA 8-inch two pegs along the same Australian rack. _(A03-S9, A04-S4, A04-S8, A04-S6)_

If APLA's real dates differ materially, the load-bearing kill weakens and OPP-04 returns as a live EXPLORE - so a person who knows the seasonal calendar can overturn this gate in one meeting, and only a person can.
- Whether Nike is willing to enter a market where it holds no rights position at all - no NBL on-court (Champion), no national teams (iAthletic since 2021, new uniforms August 2026), no Boomers sponsorship (Foot Locker) - and whether participation-and-fandom-led entry without an on-court surround is an acceptable brand posture for Basketball in a Tier-2 market. _(brand context)_ — The machine scored right-to-win 2 on the rights facts, but whether Nike Basketball plays in a country it does not dress is a brand-positioning stance, not a scoring output. It also depends on rights-negotiation intelligence - Champion's and iAthletic's contract terms and renewal windows - that exists nowhere in this base.
- Whether the Australian sell-through pull is worth commissioning at all, and if so whether it belongs to OPP-02's owner as an instrumented lead door or to a standing Australian programme. The chair decided it is a phone call folded into OPP-02; the commercial planner voted EXPLORE and would make it a programme (disagreement D-06, preserved unresolved). _(organizational knowledge)_ — Whether the account teams at Rebel and JD AU will actually release door-level sell-through, what it costs in relationship capital, and who inside APLA owns the ask are facts about the organisation and its trading relationships. Nothing in 58 signals speaks to them, and the machine's own confidence on the pull's feasibility is only Medium.
- Whether an honest but unremarkable wet-state UPF result is still worth owning as a Nike-first published measurement. The machine judges the likeliest branch to be 'holds at 50+, changes nothing commercially', and treats that as a reason to kill the mark. _(creative ambition)_ — Whether being the brand that publishes a number nobody else publishes builds equity even when the number is boring is a taste-and-ambition call about how Nike wants to argue for product truth. There is no evidence in any market that a published claim has ever sold a basketball short, and the absence of evidence cannot settle an ambition question.
- Whether Australia's participation growth in the female cohort - 450,000+ women and girls on the back of She Hoops - is strategically interesting enough to pursue on intuition, given that the machine cannot connect it to a single shorts unit and that WNBL and club team-order channels may absorb most of the bottoms demand before it reaches a retail shelf. _(intuition)_ — The base contains participation counts and zero conversion evidence, and the conversion question - does a growing player pool buy performance shorts at retail - is exactly the one Nike Greater China already answered badly (apparel units -8% while participation grew). Reading whether Australia behaves differently is a merchant's feel, not an inference the data supports.
- Whether the linerless construction decision ships regardless of this gate's outcome. Three disciplines want the sewn-in brief deleted and rules permit it, and the deletion is what funds the seam and dimensional-stability work - but layering prevalence outside elite play is a hypothesis, and if it is low, consumers read the deletion as cheapening rather than as performance. _(product taste)_ — How a consumer reads a removed liner - upgrade or cost-out - is a product-taste and brand-perception judgment. The machine can cite the physiology (0.00-1.33 kg of trapped sweat) and the rules clearance, but cannot predict the read, and the cheap test it proposes (broadcast coding and a court-side count) has not been run.

**If selected:** If the human PLM / Design team overrides the WATCH and selects OPP-04, the first and only next step is the human's call to confirm the actual APLA SS28 line-lock and futures-close dates against a September/October 2027 Australian delivery - because if that read genuinely lands after the buy closes, the programme has no rationale and should be re-aimed at SS29 or replaced by the free eight-quarter Nike AU sell-through pull; everything else in the brief is downstream of that one calendar page.

### OPP-01 — Like-Colored (REJECT)

**What the machine knows**
- [FACT] NFHS Rule 3-4-5 requires uniform bottoms to be like-coloured while permitting teammates to wear different STYLES (shorts, skirts, pants) without a state-association accommodation request, and its published rationale is explicitly about making it easier for coaches and ADs to address individual athlete needs WHEN ORDERING UNIFORMS. It dates to the 2023-24 rules cycle (announced 15 May 2023), NOT 2025-26 as the synthesis claimed - the development agent broke its own why-now and the challenger independently re-confirmed the date from NFHS and KHSAA sources. _(A06-S3)_
- [FACT] NFHS regulates tights as a separate accessory class keyed to the JERSEY - permitted only in white, black, beige or the predominant jersey colour, identical across teammates - so the legally binding colour pairs are short-to-pant and jersey-to-tight. The spec's headline engineering tolerance (dE <= 1.0 short-to-tight), which it calls 'the entire product', is therefore engineered against a pair no cited rule regulates, and for most rosters the compliant tight is black, white or beige. _(A06-S3)_
- [FACT] The trade channel was explicitly briefed on the rule change: the National Sporting Goods Association published a dealer-facing article in 2023 titled 'Player Uniforms, Apparel Impacted by High School Basketball Rules Changes for 2023-24'. Three full ordering cycles have therefore passed with the rule known to dealers and no evident stock product from any brand. _(A06-S3)_
- [FACT] Basketball is a lateral-load sport - up to roughly 450 lateral movements and 42-56 jumps per game, 31% of game actions lateral shuffling, an activity change every 2-4 seconds - confirmed against a Sports Medicine 2017 systematic review and a 2022 MDPI study of 140 professional and collegiate players. This is the best-evidenced signal in all 58 and it survived both its skeptic and the red team untouched; it makes 'validate fit in a defensive stance, not standing' a spec rather than a preference. _(A06-S1)_
- [FACT] Nike's own closest existing garment, the Pro Dri-FIT Men's 3/4-Length Tight, lists at USD 37 and street-prices USD 26.97-32.00 - at or BELOW the USD 30-36 team-dealer NET the spec proposes. A no-minimum custom supplier also exists (custom basketball leggings from USD 47.88, no minimums, free US shipping), so neither the price argument nor the minimum-order switching argument holds as written against the USD 41.99 / 8-unit Hoops King ceiling the spec set. _(A06-S3, A04-S9)_
- [FACT] The addressable ROSTER base is real and countable - 540,704 boys and 356,240 girls in US high-school basketball (NFHS 2024-25 participation survey) - but the addressable NEED (the subset of athletes wanting a bottom other than the team short) has never been counted by anyone in this base or in anything the pipeline could reach. ### OPP-05 — Continental (REJECT)

**What the machine knows**
- [FACT] EU Directive (EU) 2024/825 (EmpCo) applies from 27 September 2026 - roughly three weeks after this analysis - across all 27 member states, with no transition period for products already on the market and fines up to 4% of annual turnover in the relevant member state. It bans generic environmental claims and self-created sustainability labels. The red team searched specifically for a delay, an omnibus carve-out or a postponement and found none; it also found that many member states missed the 26 March 2026 transposition deadline, so day-one national enforcement will be patchy. This is the single cleanest why-now in the whole portfolio and it holds. _(A03-S5, RT-OPP-05-EMPCO-DATE)_
- [FACT] The instrument that would have FORCED substantiation - the Green Claims Directive - was withdrawn in June 2025 over SME-burden concerns. What survives, EmpCo, amends the Unfair Commercial Practices Directive to PROHIBIT unsubstantiated claims. It is a prohibition regime, not a substantiation regime: nothing in EU law obliges any brand to publish a number, so the cheapest compliant response is to delete the sentence. The regulation therefore produces an industry floor, not a Nike asymmetry. This is retrieved red-team web evidence, not a digest signal, and it inverts the opportunity's central moat claim. _(RT-OPP-05-GREENCLAIMS-WITHDRAWN, A03-S5)_
- [FACT] Every competitor basketball short documented in the base carries exactly the claim language EmpCo targets: Jordan Diamond '100% recycled polyester fibers... eco-conscious fashion', adidas Legends 'at least 70% recycled materials', Nike Fly Crossover 'at least 75% recycled polyester'. Separately, only 26% of the 110+ Textile Exchange Polyester Challenge signatories, Nike included, met the 2025 recycled-polyester target - recycled content is an unmet pledge, not an achieved baseline. A03-S5's own conclusion is not to spend hangtag real estate on recycled percentage. _(A03-S5)_
- [FACT] The product content of Continental is already carried, at higher confidence, by two other opportunities in this same portfolio, and the spec disclosed none of the overlap. OPP-03 'Twenty Washes' (development confidence 60) already specifies a published 20-home-launder ISO 6330 / AATCC 135 dimensional-stability and seam-strength standard on the hangtag with test date, already bartacks pocket mouths and hem stress points, already demotes recycled content to a compliance line citing the same 27 September 2026 EmpCo date, is already ~70/30 wholesale-weighted, and already names UK/Germany/France as its second lead-market tier. OPP-02 'Found Outdoors' (development confidence 62) already owns the UPF/outdoor claim on the live Nike DNA UV Woven FN2659. Strip both out and Continental's disclosed incremental content is a franchise name, a European palette, a jacquard waistband and a EUR ladder the spec itself calls an analyst estimate. _(RT-OPP-05-DUPLICATION, A03-S7, A06-S4)_
- [FACT] Nike's EMEA business is the region where its promotional damage is actually measured: EMEA revenue -6% with Nike Digital -24% while working through heightened inventory, elevated promotions and markdowns, with the CFO stating marketplace conditions are unlikely to improve through at least H1 FY2027. In parallel, Nike apparel units grew only +1% with ASP growth coming from mix and already eroded by discounts. Both are VERIFIED from Nike's own disclosure / FY2026 10-K. The proposal is a governed EUR 35 markdown floor in exactly that region. _(A04-S4, A03-S9)_
- [FACT] The channel read the brief rests on is VERIFIED and points the way the brief says: Nike Digital has fallen for ten consecutive quarters (-12% in Q4 FY26) while wholesale grew 4% for both the quarter and the full year, and the European doors that merchandise basketball shorts are identifiable in the base (KICKZ, Zalando, JD Sports Europe), with KICKZ demonstrably stocking a culturally-coded Tokyo streetball label (ballaholic). New Balance grew 19% globally to USD 9.2B in 2025 with Europe +30% and 80 new doors - but that is a whole-company, all-category figure and is NOT evidence about basketball apparel. _(A02-S7, A02-S11, A02-S8, A07-S9)_
- [FACT] Europe is the evidence base's single largest hole. The cross-dataset audit found Europe/EMEA is the primary market of under 2% of surviving signals and never once a signal's primary market, entering only as a regulation (EmpCo), a discount channel (Li-Ning clearing at EUR 20 from EUR 49 via a reseller), a door list (KICKZ, Zalando) and a negative number (EMEA Digital -24%). It instructed, before ranking, that a minimum viable European read be commissioned. That instruction originates outside this brief and is not self-serving. _(AUDIT-GEOBIAS, A02-S1, A03-S7, A04-S4)_
- [PATTERN] The two European data points the base does contain both point AGAINST the brief. The only European market growth number is Grand View putting European basketball gear at 4.9% CAGR - explicitly the SLOWEST region named (and itself part of a report-mill family the skeptic demolished as one Technavio report in four vintages, so a bad number pointing the wrong way rather than a good number pointing the right way). The only registry-grade European youth participation figure is Sport England Active Lives 2024-25 showing a significant 1% DECREASE in weekly under-16 basketball players in England, against Germany's DBB at +5.26% - two federations, opposite directions, no third in the base. _(A02-S1, AUDIT-GEOBIAS)_
- [FACT] The brief's founding assertion that 'no European consumer voice exists anywhere in this base' - stated three separate times - is false against its own corpus. Two Trustpilot observations about Nike shorts sit in surviving.json, one explicitly geography-tagged 'United Kingdom': a GBP 50 pair that 'felt like a GBP 10 pair', and a GBP 45 pair bought for a son's birthday with a returns-window complaint. Both are negative, and GBP 45-50 is roughly EUR 52-58. Caveat carried honestly: undated search snippets, not confirmed as basketball shorts specifically, and no European Nike PDP could be retrieved (nike.com and zalando.de egress-blocked). _(A01-S3, A01-S9, RT-OPP-05-GBP-ANCHOR)_
- [FACT] The UV pillar is largely free and partly unverifiable. 100% polyester technical sportswear already tests at UPF 40-50+ untreated, so a certified dry UPF 50+ claim differentiates nothing on its own; and half of the signal the brief leans on was killed by its own skeptic - Nike already ships a basketball short with UVA/UVB protection, a zippered phone-sized pocket, dual side pockets and a woven face (DNA 6-inch UV Woven, FN2659). Nobody in seven specialist files audited Nike's existing EMEA basketball assortment at all. _(A06-S7, A03-S7, A06-S4, A06-S3)_

Below it sit Li-Ning Wade clearing at EUR 20 from EUR 49 through a European reseller and Decathlon's own-brand Tarmak SH500 at GBP 5.99 on sale - a European retailer's own brand, structurally more durable price pressure than a tariff-exposed import. The audit's blunt finding applies portfolio-wide: no first-party Nike commercial data anywhere in the base, no price confirmed against a retrieved page, three mutually incompatible Nike price ladders coexisting. _(A02-S5, A03-S7, AUDIT-EVIDENCE-QUALITY)_
- [FACT] The portfolio chair placed OPP-05 last of eight at overall 28.3 with the lowest confidence on the board (22), scoring product_differentiation 1 - the lowest single criterion score given to anything in the portfolio. Development confidence was 34, the lowest at development; the red team cut it to 24 and returned survives=true only for the research gate, explicitly not for the garment ('It does not survive as a product spec, a franchise, a price position or an SS28 line slot'). The evidence stack is six moderate items and one weak - not a single strong. Two of three rankers voted REJECT; the PLM director voted EXPLORE and was overridden, recorded as disagreement D-03 rather than averaged. _(PORTFOLIO-RANK-8, RT-OPP-05-VERDICT, D-03)_

**What the machine believes**
- The moat inverts: differentiating on EmpCo is differentiating against silence. Because the EU deliberately kept the prohibition instrument and dropped the substantiation one, adidas, Puma and Under Armour each clear the bar by deleting one line of hangtag copy at approximately zero cost. Nike would spend a franchise, a 27-jurisdiction claims architecture and a legal review to be loud in a market where being quiet just became the cheapest compliant posture - and the base contains no evidence, in any geography, that a published claim has ever sold a basketball short. _(basis: Red-team retrieval of the June 2025 Green Claims withdrawal plus EmpCo's UCPD-amending prohibition structure; A03-S5's own conclusion to demote recycled percentage; the audit's resolution that percentage-on-a-hangtag is commoditised; and the total absence in the base of any claim-to-purchase evidence (A03-S5's absent-review-mention inference was invalidated as correlation-as-causation).; confidence High)_
- EUR 45 is probably a DE-RATING of existing European business rather than a new mid-core rung. The brief anchors it at ~1.5x a EUR 29.95 team stock short - the entry rung, the wrong comparator. If the two UK Trustpilot observations (GBP 45-50, ~EUR 52-58) approximate Nike's live European consumer price, Continental would sit BELOW the existing core and trade it down. That is permanent margin destruction dressed as market entry, in the region with Nike's deepest measured promotional pressure. _(basis: A01-S3 and A01-S9 Trustpilot snippets versus the single KICKZ snippet; A04-S4 EMEA -6% / Digital -24%; A03-S9 apparel ASP from mix already eroded by discounts. HYPOTHESIS-grade on both sides - the snippets are undated and not confirmed as basketball shorts, and no European PDP was ever retrieved.; confidence Medium)_
- Funding Continental would mean buying the same demand twice, at lower confidence. Its durability spec, claims architecture, EmpCo rationale, wholesale-first channel logic, UV pillar and European lead markets are all pre-existing in OPP-03 (60) and OPP-02 (62). It is best read not as an eighth opportunity but as a REGIONAL EXPRESSION of OPP-03 with OPP-02's UV claim attached - which is why it belongs inside OPP-03's European tier rather than beside it in a ranking. _(basis: Direct red-team read of dev-OPP-03.json and dev-OPP-02.json against the Continental spec; the portfolio's own cannibalisation observation that four of eight briefs propose product against the same DNA/Icon rail.; confidence High)_
- The flagship unowned claim may not be publishable as specified. The wet-state UPF figure is the only genuinely differentiated claim left once A06-S7 establishes the dry claim is nearly free on polyester - but EN 13758-1/-2 and AS/NZS 4399 appear to specify dry-state testing only, with no accredited European method for UPF at saturation. If so, the wet figure could only be published against a Nike-authored protocol, which is precisely the self-created-standard posture EmpCo forecloses, and the UV pillar collapses to a certificate on a commodity property. _(basis: Red-team analyst reading of the standards, explicitly flagged as HYPOTHESIS because eur-lex and standards texts were egress-blocked; A06-S7 counter-evidence on untreated polyester UPF. Resolvable by a one-week materials-lab work order (EUR 15-30k).; confidence Low)_
- The lead-market tiering is data-availability bias, not market prioritisation. Germany leads because a POSITIVE registry number happened to be findable there (DBB +5.26% to 288,444); England is demoted to a Tier 3 specialty-only test despite carrying the base's LARGEST European participation figure (~1.1M weekly under-16 players), whose only fault is that its direction is -1%. Selecting lead markets on the sign of the one number you found is not a market plan. _(basis: Red-team comparison of the two figures, with the honest caveat that they are not like-for-like metrics (weekly participation versus club registration) and that the England figure's signal attribution is contested (it sits under rejected signal A06-S10 and is carried by the audit under A02-S1).; confidence Medium)_
- The research gate is correct but NOT cheap, and the brief overstates both its cheapness and the blind spot behind it. The marketplace specialist's own narrative shows it already ran a 'Europe/Decathlon' search and got almost nothing back - which reframes the diagnosis from 'nobody looked at Europe' (an analyst blind spot, fixable with a literature scan) to 'Europe was looked at and yielded almost no public evidence' (a data-availability problem, fixable only with paid syndicated panel and primary work, roughly EUR 120-200k for panel access alone). _(basis: Red-team read of the specialist research narrative in surviving.json; the red team's own inability to retrieve any European page (nike.com, zalando.de, kickz.com, decathlon.co.uk, basketball-bund.de, euroleaguebasketball.net all egress-blocked).; confidence Medium)_
- The genuine finding underneath the rejected garment is real and must not be rejected with it: Europe is Nike's second geography carrying under 2% of the evidence, against a EuroLeague at a fourth consecutive attendance record of 3,251,706 (+8%) and TV viewership up 82% to 122.8M. But note the same pattern the red team found in OPP-07's Pinterest terms - a spectating record is not a playing record, and the only European registry number for the organised club layer this brief targets points DOWN. Continental may be reading a fan-apparel signal as a shorts signal. _(basis: Audit geographic-bias finding plus developer-retrieved EuroLeague figures (retrieved 2026-09-03, host pages later egress-blocked and not independently re-verified); the audit's own resolution that core organised participation is the weakest layer of the participation story and 'negative in England'.; confidence Medium)_
- The 7-inch/9-inch bracket is not a sophisticated hedge against a measured uncertainty - it is bracketing an ABSENCE of measurement, and it doubles SKU count and inventory fragmentation to do it, in the region the brief itself identifies as having Nike's deepest markdown pressure. Unit share by inseam appears nowhere in seven specialist files, three skeptic rounds or the audit, in any market (portfolio disagreement D-08, carried forward unresolved). _(basis: Audit evidence_base_quality ('no unit mix by inseam'); D-08's explicit ruling that no opportunity may be built on a length assumption until that pull exists.; confidence Medium)_

**What the human must decide**
- Whether the machine's rejection is itself the error - i.e. whether Nike should CREATE in Europe as a matter of strategy even though the evidence base cannot see into Europe. The chair rejected a Europe-created franchise partly because no European evidence exists; a human may reasonably read that same absence as the reason to plant a flag rather than the reason not to. _(strategy / organizational knowledge)_ — The machine can only reject on absence of evidence, which is not evidence of absence. It has no access to Nike's EMEA P&L, its geographic creation strategy, or whether EMEA creation authority for basketball apparel exists at all - the brief lists that authority as a what-would-need-to-be-true and nothing in the base establishes it either way.
- Whether a published, testable spec is a brand proposition Nike wants to own at all - a credibility-led rather than heat-led identity. Continental's product idea is deliberately un-hyped: no athlete, no graphic, credibility as the story. The machine can show the regulation no longer forces rivals to answer it; it cannot judge whether Nike wants to make truthfulness a design language. _(brand context / creative ambition)_ — There is zero evidence in 58 signals, in any market, that a published claim drives a shorts purchase - the base is silent in BOTH directions, not negative. Whether to lead with a spec panel is a brand-identity bet no dataset here can settle, and the machine's own precedent knowledge (transparency-led apparel propositions) could not be verified this session and is explicitly not evidence.
- Whether to accept 'a regional expression of OPP-03' as the right home for Europe, or whether Europe deserves its own owner, budget line and creation brief. The machine folded Continental into OPP-03's European tier on grounds of duplication; that is an organisational design decision as much as a product one. _(organizational knowledge / strategy)_ — The machine cannot know how Nike's EMEA and Global apparel organisations actually split creation authority, budget and line-plan slots, nor whether a European tier inside a US-led make-standard programme would ever receive real attention. Folding it in is only correct if someone in EMEA owns it.
- Whether EUR 45 is above or below Nike's live European core - and therefore whether the pricing objection is fatal or backwards. The machine's price case rests on two undated Trustpilot snippets against one blocked-page KICKZ snippet. _(organizational knowledge)_ — Nobody in this pipeline retrieved a single European Nike price page; a merchant with the EMEA price file answers this in ten minutes and it may reverse the machine's most consequential price finding in either direction.
- Whether the EmpCo legal review and the European read are commissioned regardless of this rejection - and who owns them.
