The chair elevated both to portfolio-level mandated actions independent of any brief; that elevation only happens if a human assigns it. _(organizational knowledge / strategy)_ — The machine can name the deadline (27 September 2026, roughly three weeks out) and the cost bands, but cannot allocate legal counsel, panel-purchase budget or an EMEA insights owner, and cannot know what compliance work is already in flight elsewhere in Nike.
- Whether a governed EUR 35 markdown floor is a commitment Nike EMEA could actually honour for two seasons - and whether anyone would sign for it. The machine can show Nike's recent behaviour does not support it; it cannot know whether leadership would commit. _(organizational knowledge)_ — Markdown governance is a commercial-leadership commitment, not a product spec. The machine sees only the outcome (EMEA Digital -24% on elevated promotions) and has no visibility into buy-depth discipline, account terms, or who has authority to hold a floor.
- Whether the residue is worth carrying forward at all, and in which form - the EmpCo-compliant claims architecture as an EMEA-wide asset, the European colour vocabulary, or nothing. The machine rejected the franchise and named two pieces worth elevating; a human decides whether anything else in the spec is worth keeping. _(product taste / creative ambition)_ — Judging whether a European colour vocabulary or a jacquard spec waistband is a real design idea or a decoration is aesthetic judgment. The machine scored differentiation 1 on content grounds and has no basis to evaluate whether the execution could be good.

**If selected:** If the human PLM / Design team overrides the REJECT and selects OPP-05, the first move is the human's call to make, and the pipeline's recommendation is that it be the one un-run, free, internal query that determines whether there is any European gap at all - Nike's own live EMEA basketball shorts assortment, SKU count, inseam mix, EUR/GBP price ladder by market, realised ASP and full-price sell-through - paired with a same-day rack walk of three KICKZ doors and one JD Sports Europe, before any garment, price rung or claims architecture is briefed, because that single pull decides whether EUR 45 is a new rung or a de-rating and whether Nike already ships a European expression of this product.

_The engine STOPS here. No product briefing, concept development, design work, tech pack, costing, buyer conversation or deck may proceed on OPP-05 until a human PLM / Design owner explicitly selects it - and this item is REJECT, ranked 8 of 8, at confidence 22, the lowest on the board, with product_differentiation scored 1 (the lowest single criterion score in the portfolio) and three fatal red-team kills. Two of three rankers voted REJECT; the PLM director voted EXPLORE on the grounds that the ask IS a cheap research gate, and the chair upheld his substantive point while rejecting the vehicle - recorded as disagreement D-03 and NOT averaged. Selecting it means overriding that. Three cautions travel with any override. First, the moat runs backwards: the EU withdrew the substantiation instrument in June 2025 and kept the prohibition instrument, so every competitor complies by deleting one sentence at zero cost, and no evidence in any market shows a published claim ever sold a basketball short - never present the EmpCo asymmetry as a finding. Second, this is a duplicate: OPP-03 already publishes the 20-wash ISO 6330 standard and cites the same EmpCo date and the same UK/Germany/France markets, and OPP-02 already owns the UV claim on a short Nike ships today (FN2659) - funding both buys the same demand twice, at lower confidence here. Third, every price and every length in this brief is unanchored; not one European price page was ever retrieved, the sole EUR anchor is a search snippet from a blocked page and is the entry rung, and the base's only European consumer voice (two GBP 45-50 Trustpilot items) suggests EUR 45 may sit BELOW Nike's existing European core. Separately and independently of this decision: the two pieces the chair elevated to portfolio-level actions happen regardless - the EmpCo legal and hangtag/PDP review, time-critical at roughly three weeks out and required for OPP-02 and OPP-03 anyway, and the minimum viable European read the cross-dataset audit instructed before ranking. The genuine finding underneath - Europe as Nike's second geography holding under 2% of the evidence, against a EuroLeague at a fourth consecutive attendance record - must not be rejected along with the franchise._

## 4. Cross-domain patterns

Seen all at once, the seven domains are not seven independent reads of the basketball shorts market. They are roughly four underlying source-pools, re-cut seven ways, plus one genuinely strong layer nobody built on.

The four pools: (1) audited company and league disclosure - Nike's FY2026 10-K and Q4 call, Li-Ning, ANTA, adidas, Puma, Under Armour, New Balance, Dick's/Foot Locker, NBL, WNBA, Unrivaled, EuroLeague. This is the strongest material in the base and it is cross-verified, but it describes the company and the sport, never the shorts. (2) Syndicated market reports, which the audit shows are largely ONE vendor: I confirmed directly that Technavio has serially re-released the same basketball apparel report as $4.58B, $5.93B (2023-2028), $5.93B (2024-2028) and $6.32B (2024-2029), and that the 'independent' Research and Markets $6.53B is the next vintage of the same franchise. Three domains (A01-S6, A02-S1, A04-S3) cite this as convergence. It is one estimate counted four times. (3) A cluster of AI-generated and SEO commerce content - Accio (Alibaba's B2B sourcing engine), anarchylabel, northyard, compressionathlete, ericemanuelsshop, plus one Sportsverse Substack guest post of 14 April 2026 that alone supplies the WNBA numbers in A01-S5 AND the Circana/NPD footwear numbers in A01-S6. My own searches for the Circana '-11% basketball footwear' and '4% of US footwear' figures again returned nothing at source; Circana's published 2025-2026 reporting says the opposite, that performance footwear led industry growth at +6% dollars. (4) Nike's own product copy and retailer listing pages, which appear as evidence FOR a gap in one domain and as counter-evidence AGAINST the same gap in another.

The strong layer nobody built on is the physiology, biomechanics and rules evidence in A06 (S1, S2, S3). It is the only peer-reviewed, named-sample, dated material in 58 surviving signals, and it survived attack essentially intact - and it is the layer with the fewest opportunities hanging off it.

The most consequential cross-domain finding is that the same handful of numbers is doing an enormous amount of work. The WNBA's own 'Record-Setting 2024 Season' press release - one league marketing document, about a season two years old, measured against a pre-Caitlin-Clark 2023 base - is the quantitative spine of the women's opportunity in THREE domains (A01-S5, A04-S5, A05-S1), where it appears variously as +48%, +60%, +601% and +233%. It should be counted once, and in fact it should be replaced: my search found that the 2026 WNBA season set records (league-wide attendance +16%, an All-Star crowd of 19,783 that outdrew the NBA's, 73 million unique viewers at the halfway mark) AND that the CBA that the skeptics correctly flagged as a live risk has been settled, with the team salary cap raised roughly fivefold to about $7.0M. That materially changes the women's case: it converts it from 'explosive 2024 spike on a soft base, with labour risk' to a third consecutive year of growth under a new labour agreement. This is the one place where the audit makes a signal stronger rather than weaker.

The second cross-domain finding is that the same rebuttal appears in all seven skeptic reports, phrased seven different ways: no specialist audited Nike's live line. A01 proposed a women's programme Nike ships in four weeks; A02 proposed a heritage 11-inch short and a women's inseam ladder Nike already sells; A03 missed the DNA 6" UV Woven (FN2659) and the DNA 4" 2-in-1; A05 missed the WNBA Rebel Edition shorts and the Caitlin Clark line; A06 built a storage opportunity on a gap its own fourth citation closes; A07 proposed inventing Aero-FIT basketball shorts seven weeks after Nike shipped them. I verified two of these directly. The Nike DNA 6" UV Woven (FN2659) product copy states UVA and UVB protection, side pockets, 'a zippered utility pocket large enough to keep a phone secure during the game', and a woven face that 'stands up to even the toughest rebound battles' - that single SKU is the counter-evidence to the outdoor gap (A03-S7), the storage gap (A06-S4), the UPF gap (A06-S7) and the composed-outdoor-system gap (A07-S8), all four at once. And Nike's own newsroom confirms the Sabrina 4 collection (17 July 2026) introduced Aero-FIT to basketball for the first time, on a signature jersey and shorts, using open and closed mesh zones - the exact mechanism A07 proposed as new. This is not four independent white spaces. It is one un-run catalogue query, counted four times.

The third finding is geographic. Roughly half the surviving evidence is United States, about a seventh is Greater China but sourced almost entirely from outside China (European and US resellers, a JD price aggregator, 2023 state media about one Guizhou village, and a 2019 NBA public-relations estimate of 300 million players), and Europe - Nike's second geography - has not one signal where it is the primary market. My search found EuroLeague set its fourth consecutive attendance record in 2025-26 at 3.25 million, +8%, with global TV viewership up 82% to 122.8 million. None of that is in any file. Neither is Latin America, at all. Neither is the SS28 calendar: the FIBA World Cup runs in Qatar from 27 August to 12 September 2027 and the LA28 Games open 14 July 2028, inside the SS28 selling season, in Nike's home market - and the Gulf, where the World Cup lands, has zero evidence in the base beyond a UAE property blog.

What should the orchestrator take from this? Three things. The company-and-sport context is solid and should be trusted. The product-level evidence - what a basketball short costs, how many sell at each inseam, in which market, and why they come back - does not exist anywhere in this base, in any geography, which means every price position and every length recommendation in every opportunity is currently unanchored. And the contradictions that matter most (basketball growing vs shrinking; inseams shorter vs longer; China value-tier vs premium; pockets vs seams as the failure mode; frozen prices vs Nike's actual +3% apparel increase) all resolve against the same dataset Nike already owns and has not been asked for.

Three lenses produced twenty-four candidates. Merging them was mostly the work of noticing that the same garment had been named three times. Nine of the twenty-four collapsed into two ideas: an outdoor short that Nike already ships but nobody can find, and a rules-legal team bottoms system that a 2025-26 NFHS rule change made orderable for the first time. What survived is eight opportunities, and the merge itself is the finding - where three independent lenses converged, they converged on capture and architecture, not on invention.

How I clustered. First I merged by consumer-and-product, not by name. C-CONVERGENCE-4 (Outdoor Court, Found Not Invented), C-NONOBVIOUS-7 (Legible Function) and C-WHITESPACE-4 (Found Outdoors) are one move seen from three angles: an existing SKU (Nike DNA 6" UV Woven) that closes the UV, storage and abrasion gaps four domains independently declared open (A03-S7, A06-S4, A06-S7, A07-S8), failing not on capability but on legibility in a channel that is swinging to wholesale racks with no product copy (A02-S7). I then folded C-CONVERGENCE-5 (Trapped-Sweat Spec) and C-NONOBVIOUS-2 (Wet-State Spec) into it rather than keeping them separate: they name the same consumer and the same garment, and they are best read as the proof point that makes the franchise defensible - certify UPF, dry-time and dimensional stability at the 0.00-1.33 kg of sweat a basketball uniform actually traps (A06-S2), because untreated polyester already rates UPF 40-50 dry (A06-S7). That is OPP-02.

Second, the competition cluster. C-NONOBVIOUS-1 and C-WHITESPACE-2 are the same idea under the same name; C-CONVERGENCE-2 (Layer-Ready Court Short) is the core garment inside it. All three rest on the only genuinely new, dated, primary evidence in the base: NFHS Rule 3-4-5 permitting teammates to wear multiple styles of like-coloured bottoms, and FIBA's interpretation legalising compression undershorts at any length with team colour match (A06-S3). That becomes OPP-01. C-CONVERGENCE-1 (Two Books, One Block) was absorbed rather than kept - as written it targets both the competition and the free-play user at once, which fails the distinctness rule, but its architecture logic is preserved as pattern P-01 and inside OPP-01 and OPP-03.

Third, the unglamorous cluster. C-CONVERGENCE-6, C-NONOBVIOUS-4 and C-WHITESPACE-7 all point at the core men's franchise from different sides - a 67% recommend rate across 64 reviews (A04-S6), seams and shrinkage rather than pockets as the reproducible defect (A01-S3), and a liner three disciplines want deleted (A06-S6, A06-S3, A06-S2). Merged as OPP-03, with liner deletion as the funding mechanism for the seam and shrink fix, not as a separate product.

Geography merged cleanly: three Australia candidates became OPP-04, and Europe stood alone as OPP-05 because no other lens looked at it. The three event candidates became OPP-06. The two women's clusters stayed separate because they are genuinely different consumers: OPP-07 is the fan-and-day-wear lower half in fan doors, OPP-08 is the extended-size and long-inseam performance tier that the ladder currently prices as its basement.

What I dropped. C-CONVERGENCE-3 (Women's Length and Rise System) goes, as a standalone: its premise is the empty-women's-category claim the skeptics rejected three separate times (A01-O2, A02-O2, A05-O1), and Nike ships 5", 6.5", 7" and 9" women's bottoms plus Aero-FIT on a women's signature short first. Its residue - waist control on hip-first sizing (A06-S9), coverage, extended sizes - is carried in OPP-08 and OPP-01. I stripped the Aerogami reactive-vent feature from OPP-02 (three years, one jacket - a feasibility signal, not white space), the collab-and-resale premise from OPP-06 (A05-S10 is catalogue pages, not a resale market), the CunBA cultural anchor entirely (2023 evidence, inflating retellings, Li-Ning already activated), and the shoe-is-dead-so-the-short-is-the-entry-point logic from every thesis, because A01-S6 traces to one Substack post that Circana's own releases contradict.

Two contradictions travel forward unaveraged, because they are not resolvable here: inseam direction (A02-S5 against A07-S4), and Greater China as value tier or premium (A01-S7 against A02-S3 and A04-S2). And one caveat governs all eight: no shorts-level unit, price or sell-through data exists in this base in any geography. No price in this portfolio is anchored to a retrieved page. None of these should be read as a price recommendation.

- **PAT-01 Rules, biomechanics, consumer complaint and channel economics all say this is two products merchandised as one** [strong] — Four evidence pools with nothing in common converge on a line-architecture conclusion no single domain stated. Primary rulebooks require competition shorts to clear the knee and permit colour-matched compression at any length (A06-S3, A06-S6). Peer-reviewed biomechanics says fit must be validated in a lateral defensive stance and at jump-landing hip flexion, where hem and waistband bind, with activity changing every 2-4 seconds (A06-S1). Consumer and product evidence says storage is the headline feature of the free-play short and simultaneously its most resented element (A01-S3, A06-S4, A07-S8, A03-S7). Commercial evidence says the competition garment is bought through a bookings-led, low-markdown dealer channel while the free-play garment lands on a promotional wholesale floor (A04-S9, A04-S4, A02-S7). The single basketball short sold to both worlds is the root structural error; one graded block expressed as two explicitly different families is the cheapest correction. Caveat: this does not settle inseam direction, which stays contested (A02-S5 against A07-S4). Domains: athlete × consumer × commercial × product × design × marketplace. Signals: A06-S3, A06-S6, A06-S1, A06-S4, A01-S3, A04-S9, A04-S4, A02-S7, A03-S7, A07-S8, A02-S5. Feeds: OPP-01, OPP-02, OPP-03, OPP-08.

- **PAT-02 The problem is capture, not invention - and seven researchers failing to find a shipped SKU is the measurement** [strong] — A03, A06 and A07 each independently concluded that outdoor function, secure storage and UPF were unowned white space; one live inline SKU carrying UVA/UVB protection, side pockets, a phone-secure zip pocket and an abrasion claim closes all three at once (A03-S7, A06-S4, A06-S7, A07-S8). That is one un-run catalogue query counted three times, not three findings. But the surrounding evidence for a capture problem is genuinely multi-pool: Nike apparel grows on price and mix with units up 1% (A03-S9); the volume franchise sits at 3.9 stars with 67% recommending on a real sample while the step-up clears at roughly 25% off (A04-S6); Nike Digital has fallen for ten consecutive quarters while wholesale grew (A02-S7); teen apparel mindshare trails footwear mindshare by twenty points and is still falling among girls (A01-S1); Greater China apparel units fell 8% against growing participation (A04-S2). Competitors win the same shelf by printing function and place on the outside of the garment (A07-S9, A03-S7). Legibility, not capability, is the gap. Domains: product × commercial × marketplace × consumer × design × athlete. Signals: A03-S9, A04-S6, A02-S7, A01-S1, A04-S2, A03-S7, A06-S4, A06-S7, A07-S8, A01-S3, A07-S9. Feeds: OPP-02, OPP-03, OPP-05, OPP-08.

- **PAT-03 The rulebook is the only dataset in the base that actually changed, and it changed toward women, layering and the team channel** [strong] — Across the surviving signals almost everything is stable, stale or contested. Exactly two items are new, dated, primary and verified: NFHS Rule 3-4-5 for 2025-26 permitting teammates to wear multiple STYLES of like-coloured uniform bottoms so religious and personal accommodations no longer require a permission request, and FIBA's official interpretation that compression undershorts are legal at ANY length provided the team matches colour. Both sit inside A06-S3 and both were surfaced by the skeptic rather than the specialist. The non-obvious step is commercial, not technical: team bottoms are ordered by coaches through dealers against a compliance spec (A04-S9), so a rule that widens what counts as compliant is what makes a non-standard bottom orderable as stock at all. Three needs argued elsewhere from far weaker evidence converge on that opening - coverage-first and modest-dress players (A05-S8), the layering population (A06-S6), and women sized hip-first with an under-controlled waist (A06-S9) - and it lands on the consumer where Nike's mindshare erosion is concentrated (A01-S1). Domains: athlete × culture × commercial × consumer × marketplace. Signals: A06-S3, A06-S6, A06-S9, A05-S8, A04-S9, A01-S1, A02-S9. Feeds: OPP-01, OPP-08, OPP-04.

- **PAT-04 The garment is specified dry and used wet; every unresolved failure mode lives in the saturated state** [moderate] — Read across disciplines, the failure modes cluster in one physical condition nobody tested. Basketball uniforms trap 0.00-1.33 kg of sweat, rising with intensity and with a wider range than treadmill running (A06-S2). Peer-reviewed testing shows 100% polyester technical sportswear already rates UPF 40-50+ untreated - but that is a dry rating, and the open variable is what moisture does to it (A06-S7). Drawstrings slip when saturated and the waist is left to the drawcord on hip-first women's sizing (A06-S9). The reproducible consumer complaints are seam failure and shrinkage after a single wash, which is a post-wet-state defect (A01-S3, A01-S2, A04-S6). The priority use case is 27-32C humid outdoor play (A06-S5). So the entire spec conversation - GSM, UPF, abrasion, dry time - is conducted on a dry garment while the entire consumer conversation is about a soaked one. Invisible to any single specialist because the sweat number sits in sports science, UV degradation in textile chemistry, seam failure in retail reviews and humidity in climate data. Domains: athlete × consumer × product × commercial. Signals: A06-S2, A06-S7, A06-S5, A01-S3, A01-S2, A04-S6, A03-S5, A06-S9. Feeds: OPP-02, OPP-03, OPP-04.

- **PAT-05 Women's demand survives deduplication on four independent instruments; the empty-category premise does not** [strong] — The WNBA 2024 press release is one document that reached three domains and must count once. What remains is independent and still points one way: Unrivaled's verified operations - ticket revenue +204%, tickets +249%, a professional women's record crowd, and one Philadelphia night generating roughly USD 1M in tickets and USD 400,000 in merchandise (A05-S7); Australia's national participation registry showing female participation +25% since 2022 past 450,000, unconnected to any US league (A02-S9); a retailer CEO stating on his own call that basketball is coming back built around women's basketball and that boys and girls are both buying it (A04-S5); and a US teen survey showing Nike's female mindshare still declining (A01-S1). Four unrelated instruments, one direction. The same pattern kills the product premise attached to it: Nike ships ISoFly, Crossover, Fly Crossover, WNBA Victory and Rebel Fanwear shorts and Sabrina, and put Aero-FIT on a women's signature short first (A03-S6, A03-S4). The unserved job is the lower half of the fan wardrobe and a waist-and-coverage system - not an absent category. Domains: culture × marketplace × commercial × consumer × product × design × athlete. Signals: A05-S7, A02-S9, A04-S5, A01-S1, A03-S6, A07-S6, A06-S9, A05-S8, A05-S1, A01-S5, A03-S4. Feeds: OPP-07, OPP-01, OPP-04, OPP-08.

- **PAT-06 The portfolio is weighted inversely to the quality of its own evidence** [strong] — Ranking the surviving base by evidence quality rather than by stated priority inverts the portfolio. Australia is the best-verified non-US signal in the file - roughly 1.3M players, second among team participation sports, female participation +25% past 450,000, an estimated 150,000 players turned away for lack of court space, NBL attendance above 1.2M with 58-63 sellouts, and an on-court league partner that is not a performance-basketball leader (A02-S9, A05-S6) - and every skeptic correction ran in its favour. It supports one signal and no opportunity. Greater China carries the largest share of the portfolio on evidence sourced almost entirely from outside China, in Nike's worst-performing region: revenue -13% currency-neutral with apparel units -8% (A02-S2, A04-S2), Li-Ning basketball retail sales -19% amid discounting (A02-S3) with an unresolved conflict against +5% in H1 2026 (A04-S2), and e-commerce leadership flipped (A04-S11). Europe, Nike's second geography, is the primary market of zero signals and appears only as a stripped CAGR, a markdown line and a compliance deadline (A02-S1, A04-S4, A03-S5). No single specialist could see this; it appears only when the seven files are counted together. Domains: marketplace × commercial × culture × consumer × product. Signals: A02-S9, A05-S6, A02-S2, A02-S3, A04-S2, A04-S11, A02-S1, A01-S7, A05-S5, A03-S10, A04-S4. Feeds: OPP-04, OPP-05, OPP-02, OPP-06.

- **PAT-07 Full-price demand concentrates where people physically gather, while the promotional floor sits where product is planned - and a competitor proved the mechanism in another sport** [strong] — Two datasets that never meet say the same thing. Commercially, the US wholesale marketplace turned increasingly promotional with Foot Locker comps -3.6% and Nike citing elevated markdowns (A04-S4), and Nike's ASP gain is mix rather than pricing power, already partly eroded by discounts (A03-S9). Culturally, the live economy is doing the opposite: Unrivaled's Philadelphia night produced roughly USD 1M in tickets and USD 400,000 in merchandise while broadcast viewership fell 9% (A05-S7); the NBL ran a third consecutive million-plus season with 58-63 sellouts (A05-S6, A02-S9); streetball moved into stadium venues. The mechanism at scale is proven inside this base by a rival's own disclosure - adidas apparel +35% currency-neutral in a quarter on World Cup demand while its basketball fell 21% (A04-S3). Channel evidence says the resulting product must travel through wholesale and in-arena rather than as app drops (A02-S7). The SS28 calendar that would anchor this appears in none of the seven files, and the scale calibration must travel with the claim: most of these moments are small in absolute terms. Domains: commercial × culture × marketplace × design. Signals: A04-S3, A05-S7, A05-S6, A02-S9, A04-S4, A03-S9, A02-S7, A05-S10. Feeds: OPP-06, OPP-07, OPP-04.

- **PAT-08 The price ladder is inverted against three under-served consumers at once: coverage is priced as cheapness** [moderate] — The longest, most size-inclusive SKU in the men's line - the DNA Academy 11-inch, Big and Tall included - is also the cheapest at roughly USD 37, while the 6-inch sits at USD 65 and the 10-inch discounts around 38% (A02-S4, A02-S5). That single architectural fact collides with three findings none of which was read next to it: the coverage-first need among taller women and modest-dressing athletes (A05-S8), plus-size and value replenishment behaviour where AND1 runs to 5XL and is called affordable and cultural (A01-S9), and the retro lifestyle pole defined as 9 inches or longer (A05-S3). Women's plus exists only as a single SKU inside a signature line (A03-S6), and the waist on hip-first women's sizing is left to a drawcord (A06-S9). So the length three under-served groups want is the line's basement product, in the cheapest fabric, with no women's grading. Meanwhile the floor beneath is rising rather than falling under a roughly 53.5% duty stack (A04-S8). Inseam data sits in marketplace, modesty in culture, plus-size in consumer and price in commercial, so nobody plotted the line. Domains: marketplace × consumer × culture × design × product × commercial. Signals: A02-S4, A02-S5, A07-S4, A05-S8, A01-S9, A05-S3, A03-S6, A06-S9, A04-S8. Feeds: OPP-08, OPP-07, OPP-01.

- **PAT-09 The short is a top layer in a system, the sewn-in liner is the component three disciplines want deleted, and deleting it funds the fix a fourth demands** [moderate] — Independently, athlete, product and culture each described a garment worn over something else without naming the system. FIBA permits compression undershorts at any length with team colour matching, and the 2025-26 NFHS change permits multiple like-coloured bottom styles (A06-S3). Biomechanics explains why the interface matters: activity changes every 2-4 seconds across roughly 450 lateral movements and 42-56 jumps, so a waistband sliding on slick compression is a repeated failure (A06-S1). Women's hip-first sizing leaves the waist to a drawstring that slips when saturated (A06-S9, A06-S2). A regional convention already ships the answer commercially - Philippine team practice pairs a compression liner with a loose short (A03-S10) - and coverage-first players solve it with short-over-legging (A05-S8). Commercially the liner is the densest fabric mass in a garment that traps up to 1.33 kg of sweat, in a use case that is 27-32C and humid (A06-S5), on a franchise drawing seam and paper-thin complaints at a price point with limited headroom (A04-S6, A01-S3, A04-S8). Deleting a component two groups do not want funds the construction the third is complaining about. The binding unknown is prevalence: layering rates below elite level are entirely unmeasured (A06-S6). Domains: athlete × product × culture × commercial × consumer. Signals: A06-S6, A06-S3, A06-S1, A06-S2, A06-S9, A03-S10, A05-S8, A04-S6, A01-S3, A04-S8, A06-S5. Feeds: OPP-01, OPP-03, OPP-02.

- **PAT-10 Every Western competitor is retreating from performance basketball apparel exactly as wholesale becomes Nike's growth channel** [strong] — adidas basketball fell 21% in the quarter, Under Armour is separating from Curry with apparel available only through October 2026, and Puma's basketball growth is a residual with basketball absent from its stated priorities (A04-S3, A02-S8). The one riser is New Balance: +19% to USD 9.2B, apparel past USD 1B, 80 new doors, Cooper Flagg signed, and a 7-inch mesh basketball short already in Foot Locker (A02-S8). Simultaneously Nike's own channel mix inverted - wholesale +4% while Nike Digital declined for a tenth consecutive quarter (A02-S7, A04-S1). Physical shelf is opening in the doors that are growing, and in Australia the league's on-court partner is not a performance-basketball brand (A02-S9). Two countervailing facts must travel with this: the freed space is small in absolute dollars, and the doors it opens in are promotional (A04-S4). It is a share-of-shelf and full-price-productivity opportunity, not a category-growth one, and Nike's own basketball growth is footwear-weighted with no basketball-apparel disclosure anywhere (A04-S1). Domains: marketplace × commercial. Signals: A04-S3, A02-S8, A02-S7, A04-S1, A04-S4, A02-S9. Feeds: OPP-04, OPP-05, OPP-03, OPP-06.

- **PAT-11 Heat is the only functional need corroborated by physiology, institutional behaviour change and a competitor's multi-year platform commitment** [strong] — Three unrelated pools point at thermal load in outdoor basketball. Peer-reviewed measurement supplies the only garment-level number in the entire base: basketball uniforms trap 0.00-1.33 kg of sweat, rising with intensity (A06-S2). Institutional behaviour change documents the consequence independently in the Philippines, where athletic meets moved away from 9am-3pm from 2024 and one 2024 provincial meet recorded more heat-related than sports-related injuries (A06-S5). Competitor commitment corroborates commercially: Li-Ning's Wade UPF 50+ / AT Dry platform runs across consistent style codes from Spring 2023 through 2025 at a price far below Nike's, and nike.com.cn already runs an outdoor section (A03-S7). Nike's own innovation direction agrees - cooling is its declared apparel vector and has now shipped into basketball (A03-S4). No two of these share a source. What none establishes is price, or that Nike's existing polyester does not already deliver the UPF claim dry (A06-S7), and every sweat measurement in hand is from air-conditioned North American gyms while the target play is hot and humid. Domains: athlete × product × design × consumer. Signals: A06-S2, A06-S5, A06-S7, A03-S7, A03-S4, A01-S7. Feeds: OPP-02, OPP-04, OPP-06.

### Orchestrator lens: convergence

Seven specialists produced fifty-eight surviving signals, but the audit shows they were not seven independent reads. Four source-pools were re-cut seven ways, and where three domains agreed they were usually reading the same document: one Technavio report in four vintages, one WNBA press release laundered three ways, one 2019 NBA PR estimate of 300 million players, one Nike PDP cited on both sides of the same gap. So the first job of a convergence lens is subtractive: strip the duplicate-as-corroboration, then see what still stands with independent evidence pointing the same way.

What survives that test is not what the domain opportunities assumed. Five genuinely independent evidence pools exist here: audited company and league disclosure; peer-reviewed physiology, biomechanics and primary rulebooks (A06-S1, A06-S2, A06-S3); verified event and participation operations (A05-S6, A05-S7, A02-S9); live product catalogue observation; and thin consumer-review corpora. Real convergence is where three or more of those pools point the same way about the same garment.

The strongest such convergence is structural, not a feature. The rules layer says competition shorts must clear the knee, carry no pockets and colour-match compression at any length (A06-S3, A06-S6). The biomechanics layer says fit must be validated in a lateral defensive stance, not standing (A06-S1). The consumer layer says the pocket is simultaneously the headline feature and the resented one (A01-S3, A06-S4). The commercial layer says the uniform channel is a separate, bookings-led, low-markdown pool (A04-S9). Four independent pools converge on one conclusion no single specialist stated: this is two products with one graded block, and the line is currently sold as one product to both. That is P-CONVERGENCE-1, and it reframes almost everything downstream.

The second convergence is uncomfortable. Nike's apparel grows on price and mix, not units (A03-S9); its volume short clears at 25 percent off with a 67 percent recommend rate (A04-S6); the reproducible defect is seams and shrinkage, not pockets (A01-S3); teen apparel mindshare is 26 percent against 46 percent in footwear (A01-S1); and four domains failed to find a SKU Nike ships with UV, a phone-secure zip pocket and a durability claim (A03-S7, A06-S4, A06-S7, A07-S8). Independently sourced, these say the same thing: Nike's basketball shorts problem is discovery, make quality and merchandising, not invention. The most valuable candidates in this portfolio are therefore unglamorous.

The third convergence is women's, and it must be rebuilt rather than repeated. Strip the WNBA release and what remains is independent: Unrivaled's verified event economics (A05-S7), Australia's registry-grade female participation (A02-S9), a retailer CEO's first-party call quote naming cross-gender demand (A04-S5), and a live product read showing Nike already ships the assortment the files call empty (A03-S6, A07-S6). The demand is real and sustained; the whitespace is a length-and-rise system, not a category.

Two contradictions must travel forward unaveraged: inseam direction (A02-S5 against A07-S4) and China as growth versus contraction (A01-S7 against A02-S2, A02-S3, A04-S2). And one honest caveat governs every candidate below: no shorts-level unit, price or sell-through data exists in this base in any geography, so nothing here should carry a price recommendation.

- **C-CONVERGENCE-1 Two Books, One Block** — Split the basketball shorts line into an explicitly rules-governed Competition family and an unregulated Free-Play family built on one shared graded block, so that storage, hem and liner decisions stop being compromises made against two incompatible users. _Intersection:_ Athlete/rules and biomechanics x Commercial channel economics x Consumer complaint evidence x Product and design line architecture. _Why hard to see:_ The four inputs live with four different owners. The rules interpretation sits in team-sports compliance; the biomechanics sits in sports research; the pocket complaint sits in DTC review and returns data; the low-markdown bookings economics sit in a B2B P&L nobody in mall merchandising reads. A single PLM sees one 'basketball shorts' line and one blended margin, so the two users average into a compromise garment. It took six domains disagreeing about pockets and hems to reveal that they were describing two different products.
- **C-CONVERGENCE-2 Layer-Ready Court Short** — A linerless, knee-clearing competition short engineered as a top layer over compression - with a defined non-slip waistband interface, colour-matched to the tight - turning the one rules fact and the one physiology dataset nobody built on into a system Nike alone can sell complete. _Intersection:_ Athlete/biomechanics and FIBA rule interpretation x Product/regional market convention x Culture/coverage need x Commercial team channel. _Why hard to see:_ Compression tights and shorts are different franchises with different PLMs, different fabric platforms and different margin structures, so nobody owns the interface between them. The enabling rule text is in an officials' interpretation document, not a trend report. And the strongest commercial precedent - the Philippine convention of pairing a compression liner with a loose short - is invisible from a US line-planning desk and appears in this base only as a footnote inside a price signal.
- **C-CONVERGENCE-3 Women's Length and Rise System** — Not a new women's short but a women's block offered as a system - multiple inseams, a rise option, symmetric secure pockets and an adjustable waist - sold against a rule change that now explicitly permits teammates to wear different styles of like-coloured bottoms. _Intersection:_ Athlete/fit and rules x Commercial/retailer demand x Culture/coverage and event demand x Product and design catalogue reality. _Why hard to see:_ Every domain that looked at this described it as an empty category, and a live catalogue count shows it is not - so a PLM checking the claim finds it false and drops the whole thing, throwing out the real finding with the false one. The genuine opening is only visible when the fit data (hip-first sizing leaves the waist under-controlled), the rule change (NFHS multiple like-coloured styles), the coverage need and the actual SKU list are read together. Three of those four sit outside product entirely, and the rule change sits in an officials' manual.
- **C-CONVERGENCE-4 Outdoor Court, Found Not Invented** — Nike already ships a short with UV protection, a phone-secure zip pocket and an abrasion claim, and four domains could not find it - so the outdoor opportunity is to name, spec-prove and merchandise an Outdoor Court family from existing capability rather than to invent one. _Intersection:_ Product catalogue reality x Athlete/heat and UV physiology x Commercial/Greater China capture failure x Design system language. _Why hard to see:_ This is the single clearest artefact of the convergence lens: A03, A06 and A07 each independently concluded that outdoor function, secure storage and UPF were unowned white space, and all three were wrong for the same reason - each reasoned from the absence of a term in its own search to the absence of a product in the market. No individual PLM would see this either, because the SKU is real but is merchandised nowhere near the outdoor conversation and appears in no China outdoor assortment. It takes four domains failing identically to reveal that the gap is internal discovery, not external whitespace.
- **C-CONVERGENCE-5 Trapped-Sweat Spec** — Specify the hot-market short against the one garment-level physiology number in the entire evidence base - the 0 to 1.33 kg of sweat a basketball uniform actually traps - turning 'breathable' from a marketing adjective into a published, testable claim that Nike's cooling platform can be measured against. _Intersection:_ Athlete/peer-reviewed physiology x Athlete/institutional heat behaviour x Product/Nike innovation platform x Product/competitor platform commitment. _Why hard to see:_ The number sits in a 2017 sports-medicine paper measuring sweat trapped in basketball uniforms - not a document any PLM, designer or trend analyst reads, and one that even the athlete specialist cited without using. The domain that found it built its recommendation on whole-body sweat rate instead, which is a physiology metric, not a garment metric. Only reading the physiology, the Philippine institutional evidence, the competitor platform and Nike's own tech roadmap together makes it obvious that everyone is arguing about cooling with no shared unit of measurement.
- **C-CONVERGENCE-6 Make-Quality Reset on the Volume Franchise** — The highest-certainty margin and brand-trust return in this portfolio is not a new short but fixing seam construction and post-wash dimensional stability on the franchise that carries the units, because four unrelated evidence streams say the volume short is losing full-price productivity on make, not on design. _Intersection:_ Consumer review corpus x Commercial markdown and margin x Product financial composition x Marketplace price-floor dynamics. _Why hard to see:_ The four inputs are owned by four functions that do not meet: review sentiment sits with consumer experience, markdown depth with sales, fabric GSM history with materials, and the composition of ASP growth with finance. Each on its own looks like noise - a bad review, a seasonal markdown, a mix effect. Read together they describe a franchise being cost-engineered into complaints while the marketplace trains consumers to wait for 25 percent off. It is also the least exciting candidate in the portfolio, which is exactly why no domain proposed it as its lead opportunity.
- **C-CONVERGENCE-7 Australia First, Not China First** — Land the Worldball product in the market where the evidence is strongest rather than where the priority space points - Australia has registry-grade participation growth, a verified league, a non-performance on-court incumbent and Nike's existing doors, while every Greater China price and scale input in this base is displaced at source. _Intersection:_ Marketplace/national participation registry x Culture/verified live-event operations x Commercial/competitive retreat and regional business reality. _Why hard to see:_ Portfolio attention follows the stated priority space, and no individual specialist compares evidence QUALITY across geographies - each simply reports what its own searches returned. It takes counting the base by primary geography and by source provenance to see that roughly three quarters of it is US-derived, that the China narrative is assembled almost entirely from non-Chinese sources with no Chinese price observation anywhere, and that the single best-verified non-US market supports one signal and no opportunity at all. That is a structural bias in the research, invisible from inside any one domain.
- **C-CONVERGENCE-8 Court-Day Capsule, Sized to Attendance** — Build a repeatable shorts-first capsule format anchored to live basketball events and sized honestly to verified attendance, using the one competitor proof that event-driven apparel demand is real and large - and sell it through wholesale and in-arena, not through an app. _Intersection:_ Commercial/competitor event-lift mechanism x Culture/verified live-event operations x Marketplace/channel reality. _Why hard to see:_ The mechanism evidence is in a competitor's earnings commentary about football; the occasion evidence is in league attendance releases; the channel constraint is in Nike's own 10-K. Nothing connects them inside a single domain, and the culture specialist that owned the occasion had no access to the commercial proof that the mechanism works. A PLM would also reasonably dismiss the occasion evidence on scale - until the competitor's number shows how large the lift can be when the event is large enough.

### Orchestrator lens: NON-OBVIOUS

Seven specialists produced seven maps of the same territory, and the cross-dataset audit showed most of them were tracing the same four source-pools. The value left on the table is therefore not inside any one domain. It is in the pairs of facts that no single domain could hold at once, and I hunted specifically for pairs whose halves come from disciplines that never meet: a federation rulebook and a B2B channel P&L; a sweat-physiology paper and a claims regulation; a national participation registry and a sun-protection standard; a competitor's football quarter and a basketball line plan.

Four things fell out.

First, the rulebook is the only thing in this entire evidence base that actually CHANGED. Fifty-eight surviving signals describe stable conditions, stale numbers or contested trends. Two items are new, dated, primary and verified - NFHS Rule 3-4-5 for 2025-26, permitting teammates to wear multiple STYLES of like-coloured uniform bottoms (shorts, pants, skirts), and FIBA's official interpretation that compression undershorts are legal at ANY length provided the team matches colour. Both surfaced inside A06-S3, and both were found by the skeptic rather than the specialist. They matter for a commercial reason no athlete analyst would reach for: uniform bottoms are ordered by coaches through team dealers against a compliance spec (A04-S9). Before the change, a longer or different bottom was a per-athlete permission request, which is un-orderable as a stock SKU. After it, a like-coloured multi-style bottoms family is orderable. That converts the coverage-first need (A05-S8) and the layering behaviour (A06-S6) from consumer preferences into channel-legal product, and it lands squarely on the consumer group where Nike's mindshare fell hardest (A01-S1).

Second, everything in this base is specified dry and used wet. Basketball uniforms trap 0.00-1.33 kg of sweat, rising with intensity (A06-S2). Polyester's UPF 40-50 rating is a dry-state measurement, and the single peer-reviewed paper on the subject is about what moisture does to it (A06-S7). Drawstrings slip when saturated; the reproducible consumer complaints are seams and shrinkage after laundering (A01-S3, A01-S2). The wet garment is the object nobody has tested, and it is the one place a performance claim would still be defensible as claims regimes tighten (A03-S5).

Third, the white spaces were visibility failures, not product gaps. The DNA UV Woven already carries UV protection, a phone-secure zip pocket and a durability claim (A03-S7, A06-S4, A07-S8) - and seven diligent researchers with full search access could not find it. That is a hard measurement of invisibility. Local labels win precisely by printing their function and their place on the OUTSIDE of the garment (A07-S9), while the channel swings to wholesale racks that carry no product copy at all (A02-S7).

Fourth, the portfolio is weighted inversely to its evidence. Australia is the best-verified non-US market in the base and supports no opportunity (A02-S9); Greater China carries the most opportunities and not one retrieved Chinese price (A02-S2, A02-S3, A04-S2). I have written candidates against that inversion rather than around it.

Every candidate below is a hypothesis, not a finding. Where the evidence argues against it, I have named the signal that does so rather than averaging it away.

- **C-NONOBVIOUS-1 Like-Coloured: a rules-legal team bottoms system, not a team short** — A 2025-26 US high-school rule change made multiple STYLES of like-coloured uniform bottoms legal on the same team for the first time, which converts coverage, modesty and layering from per-athlete permission requests into an orderable team-dealer SKU family - so Nike should sell a colour-matched bottoms SYSTEM (game short, 3/4 tight, full-length pant) rather than a better team short. _Intersection:_ sports-governance rulebooks x team-dealer channel economics x women's and modest-dress fit need. _Why hard to see:_ It requires reading an NFHS rules-change release and a B2B distributor's bookings economics in the same sentence. The rule change appears in this base only as skeptic counter-evidence inside an athlete signal about rulebooks (A06-S3); the channel fact sits in a commercial signal that contains no basketball-shorts data at all (A04-S9); the human need sits in a culture signal built on 2014-2017 evidence (A05-S8). Every specialist that touched one of these treated it as background. A PLM reading any single domain file would see a rules constraint, a distributor profile, or an inclusion story - never a demand-enabling event.
- **C-NONOBVIOUS-2 Wet-State Spec: sun and heat protection certified soaked, not dry** — Polyester basketball shorts already test UPF 40-50+ untreated when dry, so the only defensible sun-and-heat claim left is a wet-state one - certify UPF, dry-time and dimensional stability at the 1.33 kg of sweat the garment actually traps, and own a spec no competitor currently states. _Intersection:_ sweat physiology x textile UV chemistry x tightening environmental-and-performance claims regulation. _Why hard to see:_ The two halves live in different literatures that never cite each other. The trapped-sweat number (0.00-1.33 kg, intensity-dependent) is buried in a physiology paper that A06 cited by title and never used; the observation that polyester is already UPF 40-50 dry and that moisture is the open variable comes from a textile-science paper that only surfaced as skeptic counter-evidence against A06-S7. Read separately, one says 'basketball is a moderate-sweat sport' and the other says 'UPF is free on polyester' - two reasons NOT to build a product. Read together, they say the entire category's sun claim is measured in a state the consumer is never in.
- **C-NONOBVIOUS-3 Southern Court: Australia-first outdoor programme, then Sun Belt and Gulf** — Australia is the only market in the entire evidence base where verified participation growth, an existing consumer literacy for sun protection, a national UPF testing standard, a non-performance on-court incumbent and a league at real attendance scale all coexist - which makes it the correct proving ground for the Worldball outdoor short, not China. _Intersection:_ national participation registry x sun-protection culture and certification standard x competitor weakness in a league property. _Why hard to see:_ Australia appears in exactly one signal across seven files and supports zero opportunities, so no domain had a reason to look at it twice. The facts that make it decisive are split four ways: participation and the Champion gap sit in marketplace, the sun-protection culture and the ARPANSA UPF 50+ standard sit in an athlete signal that concludes UPF is nearly worthless, the attendance scale sits in culture, and the channel shape sits in commercial. Each domain saw a fragment that looked minor; only the stack looks like a market. The audit found the same inversion independently.
- **C-NONOBVIOUS-4 Delete the Liner, Buy the Seam: a linerless core reset funded by a component nobody wants** — The sewn-in brief liner is redundant for players who layer compression (explicitly rules-legal at any length) and actively harmful for hot-humid outdoor play, so removing it releases cost and wet-weight inside a frozen sub-USD-100 price ladder and pays for the seam construction and dimensional stability that are the actual reproducible consumer complaints. _Intersection:_ elite layering behaviour and FIBA rules interpretation x sweat-trapping garment physiology x a frozen price ladder and a documented quality complaint. _Why hard to see:_ The liner is invisible in every domain that matters. Athlete intelligence saw layering behaviour but framed it as a fit and waistband-grip problem (A06-S6). Commercial saw a markdown and a durability complaint and reached for fabric GSM (A04-S6, A04-O3). Nobody costed the liner, and nobody noticed that the physiological argument for removing it (trapped sweat mass, heat in 28-32C humidity), the competitive-rules argument for removing it (FIBA permits compression undershorts at any length with colour matching), and the P&L argument for removing it all point at the same component from three unconnected files.
- **C-NONOBVIOUS-5 The Game-Day Bottom: the missing half of a jersey outfit, sold in fan and event doors** — The women's basketball demand signal is jersey-led, not shorts-led, and the fastest-growing search behaviour is people trying to assemble an OUTFIT around a replica jersey - so the opportunity is a bottom engineered to make an oversized jersey look intentional, merchandised and priced as fan-and-event product rather than on the performance wall. _Intersection:_ platform search-and-save behaviour x live-event merchandise economics x a performance SKU's actual reported use occasion. _Why hard to see:_ It requires reading the Pinterest data AGAINST the inference the culture domain drew from it. A05 used jersey-search growth as evidence that consumers want shorts (A05-T2); the strongest term in the dataset (+494%) is for jersey outfits, which argues for tops. The correct reading only appears when that is put next to a product-domain review finding buried in skeptic counter-evidence - that Sabrina buyers wear the shorts at home rather than on court, so the USD 65 willingness-to-pay is lifestyle-driven - and next to an event-retail number the culture specialist missed entirely. Three files each held one third of the insight and each drew a performance conclusion from it.
- **C-NONOBVIOUS-6 Coverage Tier: re-tier the long inseam instead of treating it as the basement** — Nike's longest, most size-inclusive inseam is also its cheapest, which prices coverage as cheapness for the three groups that most want it - so build a properly constructed 9-11 inch tier in heavyweight mesh with women's grading and extended sizes, and stop letting the retro pole, the modesty need and the plus-size player share the discount rack. _Intersection:_ inseam price architecture x modest-dress and coverage-first need x plus-size and value replenishment behaviour. _Why hard to see:_ The four facts are each unremarkable alone and only the arrangement is interesting. The 11-inch-at-USD-37 datapoint appears only as skeptic counter-evidence inside two different domains' inseam arguments (A02-S5, A07-S4), where it was used to refute a 'design at the poles' recommendation, not to reveal a pricing inversion. The modesty need sits in a culture signal whose evidence is a decade stale. The plus-size behaviour sits in a consumer signal built on unranked Amazon listings. No domain owns 'price by inseam' as a question, so nobody plotted the line.
- **C-NONOBVIOUS-7 Legible Function: make the outdoor short readable at three metres on a wholesale rack** — Nike already ships an outdoor short with UV protection, a phone-secure zip pocket and a durability claim, and seven professional researchers could not find it - so the product problem is not capability but legibility, and the fix is a named outdoor sub-franchise whose abrasion panel, vent zone and pocket ARE the graphic, engineered for a rack with no product copy. _Intersection:_ an unfindable shipped SKU x the wholesale channel swing x local streetball labels that print function and place on the outside. _Why hard to see:_ The evidence for it is a negative result distributed across four files, and negatives are invisible to the person producing them. Three domains independently declared an outdoor, storage or UV white space (A03-S7, A06-S4, A07-S8) using the same absent-from-my-snippets reasoning; a fourth domain observed that local labels lead with pockets and place (A07-S9) without connecting it to why Nike's equivalent product was unfindable; a fifth noted the wholesale swing (A02-S7) as a bookings issue. The insight only exists at the level of the whole exercise: the failure of seven researchers is itself the data, and no single researcher could observe their own blind spot.
- **C-NONOBVIOUS-8 Heat Window: an event-anchored full-price capsule engineered for a late-summer Gulf tournament** — The only proven antidote in this evidence base to a promotional apparel floor is a major-event story - a competitor grew apparel 35% in one quarter on World Cup demand while its basketball fell 21% - and the SS28 window contains a basketball world championship in the Gulf in late August plus a home Games, so the full-price shorts moment is an event capsule that must also survive 35C-plus heat. _Intersection:_ a competitor's football-quarter financials x the promotional floor in US wholesale x heat physiology in a market with essentially zero evidence in the base. _Why hard to see:_ Not one of seven specialist files mentions the SS28 calendar, and the audit had to supply it - which means the connection is literally absent from the signal base rather than merely unmade. Worse, the proof of the mechanism was sitting inside the commercial file as a competitor datapoint about FOOTBALL, filed under 'competitors are retreating from basketball', so the one number that shows how to beat a promotional floor was read as evidence about a rival's weakness. A basketball PLM has no reason to read adidas's football apparel quarter, and a commercial analyst had no reason to read it as a calendar instruction.

### Orchestrator lens: Whitespace and Right-to-Win: opportunities defined by markets, moments, occasions, channels and price rungs that no strong player serves, crossed with demand that is already proven and assets only Nike owns.

Applying a whitespace lens to this base means first accepting that the obvious whitespace is gone. Between them the seven specialists proposed a UV outdoor short, a secure-storage short, a heritage 11-inch short, a women's inseam ladder and an Aero-FIT basketball short. Nike ships all five (A03-S7, A06-S4, A07-S8, A03-S6, A03-S4). The cross-dataset audit is right that this is one un-run catalogue query counted four times. Genuine whitespace here is therefore not 'a product nobody makes'. It is a market nobody looked at, a moment nobody planned for, an occasion a rule change just created, a channel that prices differently, and rungs of the ladder where extended sizing and durability proof do not exist at full price.

Four kinds survive contact with the audit.

Geography. Roughly three quarters of the base is US-derived. Europe, Nike's second geography, has no signal where it is the primary market, yet Li-Ning's multi-year Wade UPF 50+ platform already clears at about EUR 20 through European resellers (A03-S7), ballaholic reaches Europe through KICKZ (A02-S11), and Nike's own EMEA Digital is -24% (A04-S4). Australia has the best evidence-to-attention ratio in the whole file - about 1.3M players, female participation +25%, NBL attendance 1.23M with 63 sellouts - and a league on-court partner, Champion, that is not a performance-basketball brand (A02-S9). Both are whitespace by neglect, not by absence of demand.

Calendar. The SS28 selling season contains the FIBA World Cup (Qatar, Aug-Sep 2027) and LA28. No specialist mentioned either. The mechanism is already proven inside this dataset, by a competitor: adidas apparel grew 35% currency-neutral in a quarter on World Cup demand while its basketball fell 21% (A04-S3). In a marketplace Ed Stack calls increasingly promotional (A04-S4), a dated national-team moment is the most reliable full-price argument available, and Nike holds the US Olympic outfitting rights.

Rules. NFHS Rule 3-4-5 for 2025-26 permits teammates to wear multiple styles of like-coloured uniform bottoms, and FIBA's official interpretation legalises compression undershorts at any length provided the team matches colour (A06-S3). That is the only genuinely new constraint change in 58 signals, and it opens an occasion - a matched, orderable team bottoms system - that no brand sells today, reachable through the low-markdown team-dealer channel (A04-S9).

Ladder. Nike's live ladder is inverted: the longest short, the DNA Academy 11-inch including Big and Tall, is the cheapest at about USD 37, while the 10-inch clears at roughly 38% off (A02-S4). Extended sizing exists only at the bottom rung and mostly in men's, though Sabrina carries a plus SKU (A03-S6) and AND1 runs to 5XL (A01-S9). Durability is claimed by value brands while premium sells lightness (A03-S5, A04-S6). And the commodity floor beneath Nike is rising, not falling, under a roughly 53.5% duty stack (A04-S8).

Right to win is what separates these from a startup's wish list. Each candidate leans on an asset a rival cannot rent: wholesale doors growing while Direct shrinks (A02-S7, A04-S1), a competitor field in retreat (A04-S3, A02-S8), the team-dealer channel (A04-S9), the S.T. Flare local-build precedent (A01-S7), and a live women's assortment with the Sabrina and Caitlin Clark platforms behind it (A03-S4, A03-S6).

Two contradictions are preserved, not averaged: whether Greater China is a value or a premium play (A01-S7 against A02-S3), and whether inseam demand is polarising or the middle is the business (A07-S4 against A02-S5). No price in this portfolio is anchored to a retrieved page or to sell-through; none should be read as a recommendation.

- **C-WHITESPACE-1 Continental** — A Europe-first basketball shorts programme - one 7-inch performance block and one 9-inch city block, built to a substantiated-claims standard the EU Empowering Consumers Directive rewards - taking the doors (KICKZ, Zalando, club retail) where Chinese value brands and local streetball labels are already selling and Nike has never fielded a European basketball apparel plan. _Intersection:_ Marketplace (unexamined geography with live doors) x Product (regulation-grade claim architecture) x Culture (locally coded streetball retail already reaching Europe). _Why hard to see:_ A PLM sitting in Beaverton sees Europe as an execution region, not a creation region; every research input in this programme is US-derived, so Europe never generates a brief. It also enters the file only as negatives - a markdown number and a regulation - which reads as a reason to avoid rather than a reason to build. The single strongest European fact, that a Chinese competitor's sustained outdoor platform is already clearing at EUR 20 in European reseller channels, appears inside a signal filed under Greater China (A03-S7).
- **C-WHITESPACE-2 Like-Colored** — A rules-legal team bottoms SYSTEM - a knee-clearing linerless short, a long bottom and a matched-colour compression tight and legging, orderable together in team colours with compliant logo placement - built for the occasion NFHS Rule 3-4-5 created in 2025-26 and sold through the bookings-led team-dealer channel rather than the promotional retail floor. _Intersection:_ Athlete/rules (a new, verified, dated constraint change) x Commercial (a low-markdown B2B channel) x Culture (coverage-first and modest-dress players who previously had to request permission). _Why hard to see:_ The trigger is a single line in an NFHS rules-change release - a document apparel PLMs do not read, and one the athlete specialist missed by using a diocesan PDF as a proxy. The opportunity is an assortment architecture, not a hero product, so it produces no image for a line review. And it lives in the team channel, which is usually treated as a supply obligation rather than a creation space. The three consumer needs it serves were each argued elsewhere from much weaker evidence (a 2014 quote, an SEO compression guide, a boilerplate sizing sentence), so the strong version was never assembled.
- **C-WHITESPACE-3 Doha to LA** — A moment-led shorts programme engineered against the two dated events inside the SS28 window - the FIBA World Cup in Qatar (August-September 2027) and LA28 - using national-team and host-city codes to create the full-price reason-to-buy that a promotional wholesale marketplace otherwise denies a basketball short. _Intersection:_ Commercial (a proven full-price mechanism in a promotional marketplace) x Culture (event and live-spectacle demand) x Marketplace (wholesale is the growth channel and needs bookable stories). _Why hard to see:_ PLM calendars run on seasons; federation calendars run on qualification cycles, and no one owns the join. All seven specialists missed both events. The proof of the mechanism sits in a competitor's FOOTBALL numbers inside a signal about competitor retreat, so it reads as a fact about adidas rather than a playbook for Nike. And the Gulf, where the World Cup lands, has essentially zero evidence in the base, so the market that most needs the plan looks empty rather than unstudied.
- **C-WHITESPACE-4 Found Outdoors** — Turn the DNA UV Woven from an invisible single-length SKU into Nike's outdoor basketball franchise - extend it to 7-inch and 9-inch, take it into Greater China, Southeast Asia, Australia and the Gulf, and give it the one proof point nobody in the category has: a UPF rating verified when the garment is saturated, not only when dry. _Intersection:_ Product (an existing SKU, unmerchandised) x Athlete (an unasked physiological question - UV protection under saturation) x Consumer/Marketplace (the outdoor markets where the competitive price is set). _Why hard to see:_ It presents as a merchandising failure, so no product owner claims it: four separate domains looked at the same shipped SKU and wrote it up as a gap (A03-S7, A06-S4, A06-S7, A07-S8), which pushes the organisation's instinct toward inventing rather than distributing. The genuinely open question - what saturation does to UV protection in a garment that traps up to 1.33 kg of sweat (A06-S2, A06-S7) - sits in the intersection of a physiology paper and a textile paper that no single specialist read together.
- **C-WHITESPACE-5 Southern Court** — Make Australia the pilot market for a female-led performance shorts ladder, because it is the only non-US geography in this base with verified compounding participation, a competitor vacuum on-court, and doors Nike already sells through. _Intersection:_ Marketplace (an uncontested, verified growth market) x Culture (a league and event calendar that sells out) x Product (an existing women's block plus the one UPF claim consumers there actually recognise). _Why hard to see:_ Australia is a small line inside APLA and never generates a global brief; it supports exactly one signal in 58 and no dedicated opportunity, so the portfolio's attention flows to China, which is larger and far less evidenced. The demand detail that makes the case - 150,000 players unable to participate for lack of court space, and female participation past 450,000 - surfaced only in a skeptic's correction, not in the original signal.
- **C-WHITESPACE-6 The Other Half** — Build the women's game-day LOWER half - a women's-block mesh short designed and merchandised as an outfit piece beside the jersey, not as a game short - because the demand that is now proven across three seasons is converting into tops while the shorts sit on the performance wall. _Intersection:_ Culture (fandom-as-dress, jersey-led) x Commercial (a first-party retailer demand call-out) x Product (a live women's assortment aimed at the wrong occasion). _Why hard to see:_ Three domains read the same 2024 WNBA press release and concluded the women's shorts category was empty, which is false - so the correct move (retarget the occasion) looks like the incorrect move (create the category) and gets rejected on the audit. The clue that the gap is lower-body-in-fan-doors rather than a missing product is buried in a contradiction: the strongest Pinterest term is 'female jersey outfit' at +494% (A05-S4), and Sabrina reviewers report wearing the short at home more than on court (A03-S6). Both were treated as reasons to doubt the women's case rather than as a redirection of it.
- **C-WHITESPACE-7 Twenty Washes** — Own durability as the one premium claim nobody at premium makes: a core basketball short sold on a published, third-party-verifiable wash-and-seam specification, aimed squarely at the reproducible complaint (seams and shrinkage after one wash) rather than the imagined one (pockets). _Intersection:_ Commercial (full-price productivity in a promotional marketplace) x Consumer (a mis-diagnosed failure mode) x Athlete (lateral loading is why basketball seams fail differently). _Why hard to see:_ The failure mode was mis-diagnosed inside the base: the consumer domain built a pocket-engineering recommendation on one unverified snippet, while the reproducible complaints in the same review corpus are seams and shrinkage (A01-S3, A01-S2). The one usable quality datapoint - 67% recommend across 64 reviews - was found by a skeptic, not a specialist. And a quality reset reads as a cost line, not a product line, so it has no natural sponsor in a line review.
- **C-WHITESPACE-8 Full Range** — Break the ladder inversion: offer extended sizing (through 3X/5XL and tall) and the long inseam at the TOP of the range rather than only at the USD 37 rung, so the plus, tall and big-and-tall player can buy a performance short instead of a value multipack. _Intersection:_ Marketplace (an inverted price ladder) x Consumer (a size-excluded buyer served only by value brands) x Product (blocks and plus SKUs that already exist but are not laddered). _Why hard to see:_ Size extension is treated as a size-curve decision made after the line is set, not as a whitespace with its own price and product logic, so it never surfaces as an opportunity. The evidence is also scattered across three domains as three unrelated observations: a value-brand review, a big-and-tall retailer listing, and a plus-size style number inside a signature line. Seen together they say the same thing - Nike serves extended sizes only where margin is thinnest.

### Candidates dropped at synthesis

- C-CONVERGENCE-3 — Women's Length and Rise System, dropped as a standalone opportunity. Its premise is the empty-women's-category claim the skeptics rejected three separate times (A01-O2, A02-O2 and A05-O1 are all in rejected.json for exactly this), and it is false: Nike ships Crossover 5", ISoFly 6.5" and 7", Seasonal 9", Fly Crossover, WNBA Victory and Rebel Fanwear shorts and Sabrina, and put Aero-FIT on a women's signature short first. Proposing a women's inseam ladder duplicates in-flight work weeks before the Caitlin Clark line reaches retail. The genuinely surviving residue - waist control on hip-first sizing (A06-S9), coverage length, extended sizes, and the rules change that makes mixed team bottoms orderable - is carried in OPP-08 and OPP-01, and the demand case is carried in OPP-07.
- C-CONVERGENCE-1 — Two Books, One Block, absorbed rather than kept. As written it targets the competition user and the free-play user simultaneously with one architecture, which fails the distinctness rule and would have made every other opportunity a sub-case of it. Its logic is preserved as pattern PAT-01 and inside OPP-01 (the competition family), OPP-02 (the free-play family) and OPP-03 (the shared block and the liner decision).
- C-CONVERGENCE-5, C-NONOBVIOUS-2, C-CONVERGENCE-4, C-NONOBVIOUS-7, C-WHITESPACE-4 — Five candidates, one opportunity. Trapped-Sweat Spec and Wet-State Spec are the same idea (specify and certify in the saturated state) from two lenses; Outdoor Court Found Not Invented, Legible Function and Found Outdoors are the same move from three. All five name the same consumer and the same garment, so under the distinctness rule they are one: OPP-02, with the wet-state certification as its proof point rather than as a separate product.
- C-CONVERGENCE-2, C-NONOBVIOUS-1, C-WHITESPACE-2, C-NONOBVIOUS-4, C-CONVERGENCE-6, C-WHITESPACE-7, C-CONVERGENCE-7, C-NONOBVIOUS-3, C-WHITESPACE-5, C-CONVERGENCE-8, C-NONOBVIOUS-8, C-WHITESPACE-3, C-NONOBVIOUS-5, C-WHITESPACE-6, C-NONOBVIOUS-6, C-WHITESPACE-8 — Straight duplicate merges where two or three lenses produced the same opportunity under different names: Like-Colored / Layer-Ready (OPP-01), the make-quality and liner-deletion cluster (OPP-03), the three Australia candidates (OPP-04), the three event candidates (OPP-06), the two women's game-day candidates (OPP-07), and Coverage Tier / Full Range (OPP-08). In each case the sharper framing was kept and the weaker one's distinct evidence folded in.
- A07-O1, A07-O2, A03-S3 — The Aerogami reactive-vent feature is stripped from OPP-02 and appears in no thesis. It is a June 2023 technology that in three years has shipped on nothing but one Run Division jacket; three years of non-extension reads as a cost, abrasion or wash-durability signal, not as white space (A07-S2 classified hype). Separately, no opportunity claims Aero-FIT is missing from basketball - it shipped on the Sabrina 4 collection on 17 July 2026, which is why A07-S1 and A07-O1 were rejected - and no price in this portfolio is stated as a fact, since the entire retrieved price ladder failed audit.
- A05-O3, A05-S5 — No CunBA or village-basketball cultural anchor is carried into any opportunity. Every retrievable datapoint is 2023-2024, the viewership figure inflates from 100 million (Xinhua) to 800 million to 1 billion (CGTN) for the same event - evidence of amplification, not reach - and the space is already occupied by a funded Li-Ning athlete activation. A05-S5 is classified hype; building a 2028 line against a 2023 media peak fails the rule against resting on hype-classified signals.
- A01-S6, A01-T5, A05-S10 — Two framings excluded from every thesis. First, 'the basketball shoe is dead so the short is the lifestyle entry point' - A01-S6's Circana -11% and NPD 4%-share figures trace to a single Substack guest post that neither the skeptic nor the audit could reproduce, and Circana's own releases and Nike's FY26 disclosure point the other way. Second, the collab-and-resale premise (A05-S10, classified hype): every citation is a catalogue or product page with no price, premium-over-retail or sale-volume datapoint, so it cannot carry OPP-06 or any drop strategy. Both are available as research questions, not as reasons to build.

## 5. Opportunity dossiers

### OPP-07 — The Other Half · INVEST · rank 1 · confidence 58/100

**Thesis.** Women's basketball demand is real and now durable across three seasons on four independent instruments (A05-S7, A02-S9, A04-S5, A01-S1), and it is converting into TOPS: the strongest search term in the base is 'female jersey outfit' at +494% (A05-S4), the supply chain is jersey-led (A05-S1), and Sabrina reviewers report wearing the short at home more than on court (A03-S6). The unserved job is therefore not a missing women's category - Nike ships ISoFly, Crossover, Fly Crossover, Sabrina, WNBA Victory and Rebel Fanwear shorts - it is a women's-BLOCK lower half designed and merchandised as the other half of a jersey outfit, in fan and event doors rather than on the performance wall. HYPOTHESIS: the cheapest test in the entire portfolio is splitting the Unrivaled Philadelphia USD 400,000 merchandise night by category.

**Intersection.** Platform search-and-save behaviour x live-event merchandise economics x a first-party retailer demand call-out x a performance SKU's actual reported use occasion (culture × commercial × product × consumer × marketplace; lenses: non-obvious, whitespace, convergence)

**Why an individual PLM would find this hard to see.** It requires reading the Pinterest data AGAINST the inference the culture domain drew from it: A05 used jersey-search growth as proof that consumers want shorts, when the strongest term argues for tops. The correct reading only appears next to a product-domain finding buried in skeptic counter-evidence - that Sabrina buyers wear the short at home, so the USD 65 willingness-to-pay is lifestyle-driven - and next to an event-retail number the culture specialist missed. Three files each held a third of it and each drew a performance conclusion. Three domains also read the same 2024 WNBA press release and concluded the category was empty, which is false, so the correct move (retarget the occasion) looks identical to the incorrect one (create the category) and gets rejected on audit.

| Field | Content |
| --- | --- |
| OPPORTUNITY | Women's basketball demand is now durable rather than spiky - three consecutive record seasons, a settled CBA, and event economics verified at the till (A05-S7, A04-S5, A05-S1, A01-S5) - and it is converting into TOPS. The strongest term in the entire cultural dataset is 'female jersey outfit' at +494% (A05-S4), the retail response is jersey-led (A05-S1), and the one Nike women's short with a real willingness-to-pay signal is reportedly worn at home more than on court (A03-S6). The unserved job is therefore NOT a missing women's category - Nike ships ISoFly, Crossover, Fly Crossover, Sabrina, Sabrina 4 Aero-FIT, WNBA Victory and WNBA Rebel Fanwear shorts - it is a women's-block lower half designed, proportioned and MERCHANDISED as the other half of a jersey outfit, in fan and event doors rather than on the performance wall. The move is an occasion retarget and a fixture change, not a new category. |
| TARGET CONSUMER | Primary: women and girls 16-35 in the United States who follow the WNBA, Unrivaled and NCAA women's basketball and dress that fandom daily - the buyer who already owns or is buying the jersey and has nothing that belongs with it. She buys in fan doors (Dick's/Foot Locker, WNBAStore/Fanatics, Hibbett), at events (Unrivaled tour stops, All-Star, Final Four), and on Nike's WNBA pages, not on the basketball performance grid. Secondary and explicitly carried rather than assumed: the cross-gender buyer named on the record by Dick's executive chairman Ed Stack in Q1 2026 - 'the basketball business is coming back in a really big fashion and really built around the women's basketball business, whether that's Sabrina, A'ja Wilson,' and 'boys and girls, young men and women are buying that product' (A04-S5). Third: the coverage-first minority inside the same consumer - taller players, modest-dressing athletes - who are not served by a 5-6 inch default (A05-S8). Caution to hold in view: this is exactly the cohort where Nike's own position is weakest - Piper Sandler spring 2025 showed a 13-point drop in female teen mindshare, and fall-2025 coverage attributed the subsequent 'stabilisation' to the MALE upper-income bracket while stating share among girls was still declining (A01-S1). |
| CONSUMER PROBLEM / JOB TO BE DONE | 'I have the jersey. I have nothing to wear with it that looks like it belongs.' The women's basketball fan completes her game-day and everyday fit from three unrelated places: a licensed replica top, a men's or unisex short bought a size down, and denim. Nike's women's basketball bottoms exist but are cut for play, graded off a performance block, colour-managed to a performance palette, and merchandised on the performance wall - so the short she buys is never the short that matches the jersey she just bought, and it is never in front of her at the moment she buys the top. The job is: complete the outfit, in one fixture, in one transaction, in a proportion that reads as intentional off-court. Evidence that the job is real and currently unserved: 'female jersey outfit' +494% and 'WNBA game outfits' +70% on Pinterest Summer 2026 (A05-S1, A05-S4); Front Office Sports' 'supply desert' framing of the roughly USD 4B US women's sports merchandise market with nearly 80% of respondents saying they would buy more if it existed (Klarna / Sports Innovation Lab, https://frontofficesports.com/womens-sports-merchandise-market-4-billion/, and per that reporting the Indiana Fever and Golden State Valkyries have sold denim shorts and bedazzled shirts successfully - fans will buy lifestyle bottoms, retrieved 2026-09-03); and Nike's own Sabrina reviewers reporting they wear the short at home more often than playing basketball because it is lightweight and comfortable (A03-S6). HYPOTHESIS, not fact: that jersey adjacency is the driver rather than a general athletic-shorts fashion cycle. The Fever/Valkyries denim-shorts datapoint argues the second reading as strongly as the first. |
| PRODUCT IDEA | A women's-block fan-and-everyday basketball short, built on ONE new block in TWO inseams, merchandised beside the jersey.  SILHOUETTE: High rise (natural waist, approximately +2.5cm rise over the current Nike women's Dri-FIT basketball grade) with a clean flat front so a jersey tucks without bunching; straight leg with no side-seam taper and a wide hem opening so it hangs rather than clings. This is a proportion decision, not a length decision - the point of difference is rise and leg-line, which is what makes a short read as 'outfit' rather than 'kit'.
